# art.draw: request-shape coverage (R2)

Every line is a request shape of one operation family. `supported` lines are covered by a test in `tests.sop` (ids `t.art.draw.r2<group>NN`, generated by running the line on the real engine: the reply start and the changed state are asserted). `unsupported` lines say why. Shapes: imperative, question, wish ("I want"), indirect ("it should be", "X would be nicer"), elliptic (very short), voice (fillers, run-ons), typo/abbreviation (u, pls, thx, dk, grn, whats), word-order, synonym, pronoun, quantity, negation, coordination, politeness, state questions and option questions. The general mechanisms behind them: a filler + politeness prefix (`um so like`, `hey yo could you`, `i was wondering if you could`), a trailer (`pls thx ok i guess ish`), noun lexicons (`targets`, `parts`, `preps`, `regions`, `flipwords`), and ops that accept extra adjectives for noun-first moves.

# data.charts: request-shape coverage

Every operation, every way of asking that the rules support, and the test that proves it (`tests.sop`; ids `nNN` are the original suite, `r2NNN` the R2 sweep). files.operations.sop:
@op.data.charts.fromText core.operation
    impl=fromText
    semantics=action
    action=chart.fromText
    doc="Builds a chart from numbers typed by the user (\"apples 5, pears 3\"); the numbers keep the id of the request wire."

@op.data.charts.new core.operation
    impl=newChart
    semantics=action
    action=chart.new
    doc="Starts a new empty chart and makes it the active one."

@op.data.charts.refresh core.operation
    impl=refresh
    semantics=action
    action=chart.refresh
    doc="Reads the source of the active chart again (what people have, prices, lists, legs) and updates the numbers; keeps the style."

@op.data.charts.duplicate core.operation
    impl=duplicate
    semantics=action
    action=chart.duplicate
    doc="Copies the active chart (data and style) into a new chart."

@op.data.charts.fromHoldings core.operation
    impl=fromHoldings
    semantics=action
    action=chart.fromHoldings
    doc="Builds a chart of what people have: reads the kids.arith holdings and asks the computed counts (ctx.ask count); every number comes from wires whose ids are kept in the chart source."

@op.data.charts.fromPrices core.operation
    impl=fromPrices
    semantics=action
    action=chart.fromPrices
    doc="Builds a chart of prices from the kids.shop price list (ctx.ask cost) for a group (toys, fruit, school things, snacks, drinks) or named items."

@op.data.charts.fromLegs core.operation
    impl=fromLegs
    semantics=action
    action=chart.fromLegs
    doc="Builds a chart of the number of legs from the kids.animals knowledge base (ctx.ask matching and legs) for a group of animals or named animals."

@op.data.charts.fromList core.operation
    impl=fromList
    semantics=action
    action=chart.fromList
    doc="Builds a chart from the kids.tasks entries of one list (quantities from \"3 apples\"), or the number of items on every list."

@op.data.charts.addPoint core.operation
    impl=addPoint
    semantics=action
    action=chart.addPoint
    doc="Adds one or more labelled numbers to the active chart (an existing label is changed)."

@op.data.charts.removePoint core.operation
    impl=removePoint
    semantics=action
    action=chart.removePoint
    doc="Removes one label from the active chart."

@op.data.charts.setPoint core.operation
    impl=setPoint
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setPoint
    doc="Sets the number of one label."

@op.data.charts.adjustPoint core.operation
    impl=adjustPoint
    semantics=action
    action=chart.adjustPoint
    doc="Increases, decreases, doubles, triples or halves the number of one label."

@op.data.charts.renamePoint core.operation
    impl=renamePoint
    semantics=action
    action=chart.renamePoint
    doc="Renames one label."

@op.data.charts.clearData core.operation
    impl=clearData
    semantics=action
    action=chart.clearData
    doc="Removes all data from the active chart and keeps its style."

@op.data.charts.setType core.operation
    impl=setType
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setType
    doc="Changes the type (bar, line, pie, doughnut, radar, polar area, scatter), optionally stacked; creates an empty chart when there is none."

@op.data.charts.setStacked core.operation
    impl=setStacked
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setStacked
    doc="Stacks the series or puts them side by side."

@op.data.charts.setTitle core.operation
    impl=setTitle
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setTitle
    doc="Sets the title of the active chart."

@op.data.charts.removeTitle core.operation
    impl=removeTitle
    semantics=action
    action=chart.removeTitle
    doc="Removes the title of the active chart."

@op.data.charts.setColor core.operation
    impl=setColor
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setColor
    doc="Colors the whole chart (or one label) with a named color and optional shade."

@op.data.charts.setPalette core.operation
    impl=setPalette
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setPalette
    doc="Applies a palette (rainbow, pastel, ocean, forest, sunset, warm, cool, neon, earth), different colors per bar, or the default."

@op.data.charts.setSort core.operation
    impl=setSort
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setSort
    doc="Sorts the items of the active chart (biggest first, smallest first, alphabetically) or restores the order."

@op.data.charts.setOrientation core.operation
    impl=setOrientation
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setOrientation
    doc="Makes a bar or line chart horizontal or vertical."

@op.data.charts.setValues core.operation
    impl=setValues
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setValues
    doc="Shows or hides the numbers (or percentages) on the chart."

@op.data.charts.setLegend core.operation
    impl=setLegend
    semantics=action
    action=chart.setLegend
    doc="Shows or hides the legend."

@op.data.charts.extreme core.operation
    impl=extreme
    semantics=action
    action=chart.extreme
    doc="Answers which label is the biggest or the smallest in the active chart."

@op.data.charts.total core.operation
    impl=total
    semantics=action
    action=chart.total
    doc="Answers the total of the numbers in the active chart."

@op.data.charts.average core.operation
    impl=average
    semantics=action
    action=chart.average
    doc="Answers the average of the numbers in the active chart."

@op.data.charts.difference core.operation
    impl=difference
    semantics=action
    action=chart.difference
    doc="Answers how much more or less one label is than another."

@op.data.charts.compare core.operation
    impl=compare
    semantics=action
    action=chart.compare
    doc="Answers which of two labels is bigger or smaller."

@op.data.charts.percent core.operation
    impl=percent
    semantics=action
    action=chart.percent
    doc="Answers which percentage of the total a label is."

@op.data.charts.valueOf core.operation
    impl=valueOf
    semantics=action
    action=chart.valueOf
    doc="Answers the number of one label and its share of the total."

@op.data.charts.countItems core.operation
    impl=countItems
    semantics=action
    action=chart.countItems
    doc="Answers how many items (bars, slices, points) the active chart has."

@op.data.charts.describe core.operation
    impl=describe
    semantics=action
    action=chart.describe
    doc="Describes the active chart in one text (type, title, numbers, biggest)."

@op.data.charts.read core.operation
    impl=read
    semantics=action
    action=chart.read
    doc="Reads the description of the active chart aloud (effect speech.say)."

@op.data.charts.switchChart core.operation
    impl=switchChart
    semantics=action
    action=chart.switchChart
    doc="Makes another chart the active one: by position (first, last, 2), next, previous or title."

@op.data.charts.deleteChart core.operation
    impl=deleteChart
    semantics=action
    action=chart.deleteChart
    doc="Deletes the active chart, a numbered chart or all charts."

@op.data.charts.listCharts core.operation
    impl=listCharts
    semantics=action
    action=chart.listCharts
    doc="Lists the charts with their titles and types."

@op.data.charts.download core.operation
    impl=download
    semantics=action
    action=chart.download
    doc="Saves the active chart as a picture (effect charts.download, executed by the Charts tab with canvas toDataURL)."

@op.data.charts.downloadData core.operation
    impl=downloadData
    semantics=action
    action=chart.downloadData
    doc="Downloads the numbers as a CSV file (effect file.download)."

@op.data.charts.copyData core.operation
    impl=copyData
    semantics=action
    action=chart.copyData
    doc="Copies the numbers to the clipboard (effect clipboard.copy)."

@op.data.charts.toDocument core.operation
    impl=toDocument
    semantics=action
    action=chart.toDocument
    doc="Puts the chart picture into the document: asks docs.editor for the action doc.addImage (not offered yet, so it explains)."

@op.data.charts.toDocumentData core.operation
    impl=toDocumentData
    semantics=action
    action=chart.toDocumentData
    doc="Puts the title and the numbers of the chart into the document with the documented requests doc.addHeading and doc.addList."


@op.data.charts.options core.operation
    impl=options
    semantics=action
    action=chart.options
    doc="Tells what the Charts tab can do: the chart types, colors and palettes, the settings and the questions it answers."

@op.data.charts.undo core.operation
    impl=undo
    semantics=action
    action=chart.undo
    doc="Undoes the last change to a chart (type, colours, points, titles, data); the history is kept in the world state."

@op.data.charts.redo core.operation
    impl=redo
    semantics=action
    action=chart.redo
    doc="Does the undone change again."

files.coverage.md:
# docs.editor rule coverage

**S** = supported (pattern `example=`, `tests.sop` test or `datagen.mjs` family, checked by `npm test` / `test-world`), **U** = unsupported (reason). New rows of this sweep are marked **new**.
Noise: fillers, modal and wish prefixes (`can u`, `i want`, `i need`, `hey`), suffixes (`pls`, `plz`, `thx` after free text, `for me`), ordinal and numeral variants. Digit ordinals are tokenized as `2` + `nd`, number words as digits (`paragraph two` = `paragraph 2`); patterns are written for both.

| Operation | Request shape | Status | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc.addHeading` | imperative | S | `add a heading Shopping` |
| | wish / modal (new) | S | `i want a heading that reads Shopping`, `could you insert a header named Shopping` |
| | noun last (new) | S | `add Shopping as a heading` |
| | very short | S (new) | `new heading Shopping`; bare `heading Shopping` is U (it collides with `heading list` of the reader) |
| `doc.addParagraph` | imperative | S | `add a paragraph We went to the park` |
| | wish / chat (new) | S | `i want a paragraph that says ...`, `new paragraph ... pls`, `add ... as a paragraph` |
| `doc.addList` | imperative | S | `add a list with milk, eggs and bread` |
| | chat (new) | S | `new list containing milk, eggs and bread`, `add the items milk, eggs and bread in a list`, `put milk, eggs and bread into a list pls`, `i need a list with ... on it` |
| | reordered items / canonical text | U | gold rewrites the item order or punctuation (`list: milk, eggs, bread`), not derivable |
| `doc.delete` ordinal | imperative | S | `delete the second paragraph` |
| | numerals and chat (new) | S | `delete 2nd paragraph`, `cut out the second heading`, `second paragraph should go`, `2nd paragraph delete` |
| `doc.read` ordinal / numeral | imperative | S | `read the second paragraph` |
| | numerals (new) | S | `read para 2`, `read the 2nd paragraph`, `read number two paragraph pls`, `can u read paragraph two out loud`, `say paragraph 2`, `second paragraph read please` (emitted as `n=2`) |
| | `read me the second one` | S (new) | assumes paragraph |
| `doc.goto` ordinal | imperative | S | `go to the second heading` |
| | numerals / chat (new) | S | `jump to 2nd heading`, `take me to the second heading`, `go to heading number 2`, `heading two please`, `second heading go`, `scroll to the 2nd heading` |
| `doc.select` block | imperative (new) | S | `pick the second paragraph`, `grab the second paragraph`, `select 2nd para` |
| | wish / noun first (new) | S | `i want the second paragraph selected`, `make a selection of the second paragraph` |
| | `select paragraph 2` | S | text kept as typed (`paragraph 2`) |
| `doc.select` word | imperative (new) | S | `pick the word cat`, `select the cat word`, `i want to select the word cat`, `highlight cat so i can select it` |
| `doc.whatSelected` | question (new) | S | `which bit is selected`, `what have I selected so far`, `what am I selecting`, `tell me the selection`, `what part is my selection covering`, `wat is selected atm`, `remind me what I have selected`, `which text did I pick out` |
| | two-sentence form | U | `is anything selected? what is it` is two sentences |
| `doc.format` block marks | imperative (new) | S | `bolden the second paragraph`, `bold the 2nd paragraph`, `italicize paragraph 2` |
| | chat / noun first (new) | S | `second para bold pls`, `can u make paragraph two bold`, `i want the second paragraph in bold`, `make para 2 bold please`, `hey make the second one bold` |
| `doc.format` highlight with colour | imperative | S | `highlight the word milk in green` |
| | chat / reorder (new) | S | `highlight milk green pls`, `milk green highlight`, `green highlight on milk`, `milk should be highlighted green`, `color the word milk green please`, `could you put a green highlight on milk` |
| | `make milk green` | U | `make X <colour>` is a drawing/avatar command in other worlds; only the forms with the word `word` or `highlight` are claimed |
| `doc.link` | imperative | S | `add a link to example dot com on the word example` |
| | chat / reorder (new) | S | `link example to example dot com pls`, `example should link to example dot com`, `put a link on example pointing to example dot com`, `word example link example dot com`, `hey make example link to example dot com` |
| `doc.align` | imperative | S | `center the heading` |
| | chat (new) | S | `put the heading in the center`, `i want the heading in the middle`, `middle align the heading`, `shift the heading to center alignment`, `could you line the heading up in the centre`, `heading to the middle`, `heading centred please` |
| `doc.addTable` | imperative | S | `add a table with 3 columns: animal, legs, food` |
| | chat (new) | S | `table 3 columns animal legs food`, `make a table animal legs food`, `3 column table animal legs food`, `new table animal legs food pls`; `ops.mjs` now splits column names written without commas |
| | canonical spec | U | gold normalises the spec to `3 columns: animal, legs, food`; the rules keep the user's words |
| `doc.addTask` | imperative | S | `add a task buy bread` |
| | chat (new) | S | `new task buy bread pls`, `add buy bread as a task`, `put a task buy bread in the doc`, `could you add a task called buy bread`, `task buy bread`, `todo buy bread` |
| `doc.countTasks` open | question | S | `how many tasks are left` |
| | chat / reorder (new) | S | `how many unfinished tasks are there`, `number of open tasks?`, `open tasks count pls`, `how many tasks not finished yet`, `tasks not done how many`, `how many tasks have i not done` |
| `doc.stats` | very short | S | `word count`, `wordcount pls`, `number of words in the doc?` |
| | `how many words` | S (as count) | stays `doc.count kind=word` as in the training data; `count the words` is left to docs.reader |
| other ops (clear, replace, move, title, newDoc, undo, redo, copy, download, count, mentions, isEmpty, dictate, fromList, report, holdings, rows/columns, cells, check/uncheck, rule, quote) | earlier patterns | S | unchanged (see tests) |
| negation / undo | `undo`, `redo`, `unbold`, `remove the bold from ...` | S | unchanged |

Notes: the new patterns that capture free text use `words(N)` followed by an optional `pls|plz|thx`, so a chat suffix is not captured into the text. Several shapes of the held-out labels (table spec, list item punctuation) are canonical rewrites and cannot be met by rules.

# docs.reader: request-shape coverage (R2)

Status: S = supported by rules, with a test (`tests.sop`, ids `t.docs.reader.s###` for the sweep, `nNN` for the original ones) and a generator family (`datagen.mjs`); U = unsupported, with the reason.
All patterns are `pat.docs.reader.*` (original) or `pat.docs.reader.sw.*` (sweep). Every wh-question pattern also exists with an indirect lead-in (`pat.docs.reader.ind.*`: "tell me / I want to know / I wonder / could you tell me / let me know ..." + the question).
Run-on and politeness handling: `can u / could you / hey / pls / thx / I want to / let me`, trailing `pls / now / for me / thanks`; `please/ok/well/um` are removed by the tokenizer.

Operations (docr.*): describe, summary, characters, mainCharacter, places, keywords, outline, stats, who, did, happened, where, whoV, didV, said, saying, part, sentence, count, search, searchStep, clearSearch, across, relation, isRelated, read, list, open, close, loadSample, ask.

## Shapes common to every operation

| Shape | Status | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | S | "Summarize the story." |
| question | S | "What is the story about?" |
| wish / indirect request | S | "I want a summary of the story." (summary, stats, outline, read, search); "I want to know how it ends." (all wh-questions via `ind.*`) |
| statement-as-command | U | "The story is too long, shorten it": no operation expresses intent from a statement |
| very short / elliptic | S | "tldr", "nxt", "prev", "word count", "Characters?", "Outline pls", "Unhighlight" |
| fillers, run-ons, abbreviations (u, pls, thx, whats, hw) | S | "hey can u search for oven pls", "whats sentence 5", "hw many times is hansel said" |
| typos | S/U | one-word typos are corrected by the engine (`sumarize the story`); a typo plus a lead-in ("hey can u sumarize") is not (engine retry, see report) |
| word-order variants (noun first, fragment) | S | "Section 2 summary pls", "Oven search pls", "Witch mentions count", "Start of the story?", "Hansel sister who" |
| synonyms | S | begin/start/open/opening/intro, end/finish/conclude/close, summary/recap/gist/tldr/synopsis/plot, find/search/look for/locate, story/tale/text/file/doc/book/article... |
| pronouns and references | S/U | "who is she" after a name, "the witch, who is that" S; "how are they related" U (isRelated needs two named entities) |
| numbers, ordinals, number words | S | "section two", "the second section", "sentence 5", "Summarize the story in three sentences", "one more result" |
| negation and undo | S | "no more highlights", "get rid of the highlighting", "unhighlight"; "undo the last search" U (no history of searches) |
| coordination | S | multi-command messages are split by the dispatcher/segmenter; one sentence with two intents is U ("summarize it and list the characters" goes to two segments) |
| politeness and chit-chat | S | "could you please...", "hey ...", "I'd like to..." |
| questions about state | S | "which documents do I have", "how many files do I have", "how long is it", "is there a search yet" (step with no search answers honestly) |
| questions about options | U | "what can I ask about the story?" belongs to ui.help |

## Per operation

| Operation | Shapes covered (S) | Unsupported (U) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| describe | "describe/introduce/analyse/explain/inspect the file", "what is this file", "tell me about this document", "give me an overview / info / details of the file", "what is in the file", "have a look at the file" | none known |
| summary (document) | "summarize/recap/sum up/condense/tldr", "sum it up", "summary of the story", "the gist", "short version", "what is the plot", "what is it about / whats this about", "what happens in the story", "story summary pls", "tell me the story in a nutshell", "tell me what the story is about" | "make it shorter" (not a reading operation) |
| summary k | "summarize in three sentences", "sum up the story in two lines" | k for sections ("section 2 in 2 sentences") U: the op takes n or k, not both |
| summary section | "summarize/sum up/tldr section N", "section N summary pls", "short summary of chapter N", "what is section N about / in short", "what does section N cover", "tell me about section N", ordinal forms ("the last section", "the second chapter", "the first one in short") | "page N": a document has no pages. "part N" is read as section N. Ordinals produce `arg.ord`, digits `arg.n` (a held-out label that expects `n=2` for "second" differs only in form) |
| characters | "who are / list / name / show the characters", "cast of the story", "who is in it / who appears in it", "who all is in the story", "which people appear", "characters in the story?", "I wanna know who the characters are" | "how many characters" is stats |
| mainCharacter | "who is the main character / hero / protagonist / lead", "who is the story about", "who does the story follow", "who is it about", "who is mentioned the most", "main character?" | none |
| places | "which places are mentioned", "places in the story?", "places mentioned pls", "what towns/villages/cities appear", "where does the story take place / happen", "where does the story happen, list places", "list the locations" | map display (geo.map) |
| keywords | "key words / keywords / key terms", "top/main/most common words", "what words are used the most", "what are the themes / topics" | none |
| outline | "outline", "table of contents", "headings", "chapter titles", "what are the headings", "what sections does it have", "how is it structured / laid out" | "go to the outline" (navigation) |
| stats | "word/sentence/paragraph/section count", "how many words / sentences does it have", "how long is the story (in words)", "words in the story?", "count the sentences", "number of sentences", "length in words", "show me the stats" | "reading time" as a separate question (answered inside stats) |
| sentence | "sentence 5", "line 5 please", "whats sentence 5", "sentence number 5", "show me sentence 5 pls", "read me number 5 sentence", "what is the fifth sentence" (read ord) | ranges ("sentences 5 to 8") U |
| who | "who is X / whos X / who is that X / the old X", "tell me about X", "tell me who X is", "X, who is that", "what is X like", "what kind of person is X", "what is the role of X", "what do you know about X" | none |
| did / happened / where | "what did X do", "what does X get up to", "what role does X play", "what happens to X (finally)", "what became of X", "X's fate", "how does X end up", "where does X live / go", "where X lives" | none |
| whoV / didV / saying / said | all original forms; "who said Q", "whose line is Q", "speaker of Q", "who was it that said Q", "find who said Q" (with or without quotes and "in the story") | none |
| part | beginning/start/opening/intro, end/ending/conclusion, middle: "what is the beginning like", "start of the story?", "how does the tale open", "what happens first / last", "how did it finish", "tell me how it ends", "what is the first thing that happens"; section forms "what is going on in section N", "what happens in the second chapter" | none |
| count | "how many times is X mentioned / does X appear / often does X come up", "count X", "how many mentions of X", "X mentions count", "number of X mentions", "times X is named", "X how many times", "how many times does the name X appear", typo "hw" | counting non-cast words ("how many times is the oven mentioned") has a low-priority generic pattern; "count" of a phrase with more than four words U |
| search | "find/search/look for/look up/locate/highlight X (in the story)", "find the word X", "search for the word X", "X search pls", "where does X appear", "where is X in the text", "show me where it says X", "is the word X in the story, search it", "any mentions of X in the story" | a bare "find X" without "the word"/"in the story" is U on purpose (it would claim "find the cat" of other worlds) |
| searchStep | "next result / match / hit / one", "next one please", "one more result", "nxt", "skip to the next match", "go back one result", "previous one", "jump to the first hit", "go to the last match" | "next oven" (the search word repeated) U; routed to other worlds |
| clearSearch | "clear/remove/hide/reset the highlights/marks/search", "unhighlight", "get rid of the highlighting", "turn off the search marks", "no more highlights", "remove the yellow marks", "stop highlighting" | none |
| across | "which documents mention X", "what files talk about X", "which doc has X", "is X in any of my documents", "X across documents", "docs that mention X", "in what documents is X", "can you check which documents mention X" | none |
| relation / isRelated | "who is X's sister", "who is the sister of X", "whos hansel's younger sister", "what do you know about X's sister", "how are X and Y related / connected", "what is the connection between X and Y", "are X and Y related" | possessive without apostrophe ("hansels sister") only through the original typo path; "who is the sister" (no owner) U; pronoun pairs U |
| read | "read the first paragraph", "read section 2 (aloud)", "read out the second paragraph", "show me the third paragraph", "go to section 2", "read the story / it / this to me", "read aloud", "narrate the story", "read from the start", "read out the beginning of the story" | page-based reading U |
| list | "which documents do I have", "list my docs pls", "documents list", "what files do I have here", "how many files do I have", "my docs?" | none |
| open / close / loadSample | original forms ("load the sample story", "open the example document", "close the file") | closing "all documents" U |
| ask (passage fallback) | "does the story say X", "what does the story say about X", "according to the text X", "is there a X in the story", "is a X mentioned", "does the tale have a X", "check if there is a X", "could you tell me if the story mentions a X", "does it mention X" | "X in the story?" with nothing else U on purpose (too open, collides with the editor) |

## Notes for the dialog layer

`interceptInput` in `ops.mjs` answers wh-questions of an open document before the formalizer sees them (modal input). The final passage fallback there now leaves the shapes the pattern file reads itself (`STRUCTURED_Q`) to the formalizer. Because of the interceptor, the routed evaluation (`scripts/eval-rules.mjs`) counts those texts as not parsed although the dialog answers them.

# Hansel and Gretel

> Source: a short English retelling of the fairy tale collected by the Brothers Grimm (Kinder- und Hausmärchen, 1812). The tale is in the public domain; this retelling was written for this project and is released under CC0 (public domain dedication).

## The Poor Woodcutter

Once upon a time a poor woodcutter lived at the edge of a great forest with his two children and their stepmother. The boy was called Hansel and his little sister was called Gretel. The woodcutter was their father. He loved his children, but the family had almost nothing to eat. The stepmother was cruel and she hated the children.

One evening the stepmother spoke to the father. "There is not enough bread for four," she said. "Tomorrow you must take the children deep into the forest and leave them there." The father wept, but he agreed in the end. Hansel heard every word through the thin wall of the bedroom. He told his sister about the plan. "Do not cry, Gretel," he whispered. "I will find a way."

Hansel crept out of the house at night and filled his pockets with white pebbles. In the morning the father led the children into the forest. Hansel dropped a pebble on the path every few steps. The father lit a fire and went away. The children waited until the moon rose. The white pebbles shone in the moonlight and showed them the way home. The father was glad to see them, but the stepmother was furious.

## Lost in the Forest

A few days later the stepmother made the father take the children into the forest again. This time Hansel had no pebbles, so he scattered crumbs of bread on the path. The birds ate every crumb. When night came, Hansel and Gretel were lost. They walked for three days and grew hungry and tired.

At last they saw a white bird. It led them to a little house in a clearing. The walls of the house were made of bread and the roof was made of cake. The windows were made of clear sugar. Hansel ate a piece of the roof and Gretel ate a piece of the window. "Nibble, nibble, little mouse, who is nibbling at my house?" called a voice from inside.

The door opened and an old woman came out. She was a witch, but she smiled kindly at the children. "Come in, dear children," said the witch. "You will have food and a warm bed." Hansel and Gretel followed her into the house. They did not know that the witch built her house of bread to catch hungry children.

## The Witch's Oven

Early the next morning the witch locked Hansel in a small cage. She made Gretel carry water and cook for her brother. "Fatten him up," said the witch. "I will eat him when he is fat." Every day the witch came to the cage and said, "Hansel, put out your finger so that I can feel how fat you are." Hansel held out a thin bone instead of his finger. The witch could not see well, so she thought the bone was his finger. She was angry that Hansel stayed so thin.

After four weeks the witch lost her patience. "Gretel, climb into the oven and see if it is hot enough," she ordered. Gretel guessed the witch's plan. "I do not know how," said Gretel. "Show me first." The witch bent over and put her head into the oven. Gretel pushed her with all her strength and shut the iron door. The witch burned in her own oven.

Gretel ran to the cage and set her brother free. "The witch is dead!" she cried. Hansel and Gretel hugged each other and danced with joy. They found pearls and jewels in every corner of the witch's house. They filled their pockets and their aprons and set off for home.

## Home Again

On their way they came to a wide lake. A white duck carried Hansel and Gretel across the water, one after the other. Soon they saw the woodcutter's house through the trees. They ran inside and threw their arms around their father. The father had not had a happy hour since he lost the children. The stepmother was dead. Gretel shook out her apron and the pearls rolled over the floor. From that day on the family lived together without worry, and the father was never poor again.

files.coverage.md:
# games.chess: request-shape coverage

The user plays against the built-in engine; moves are SAN-free spoken or typed squares, with questions about legality, piece locations, the board and the game.

Every line is either supported (with the example that has a test in `tests.sop`, ids `sw###`) or unsupported with the reason. Shapes: imperative, question, wish, indirect, statement-as-command, elliptic, voice/fillers, typos/abbreviations, word order, synonyms, references, quantities, negation/undo, coordination, politeness, state questions, option questions.

## move

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| elliptic | e4 | supported (test sw001) |
| imperative | Knight to f3. | supported (test sw002) |
| wish | how about d4 | supported (test sw003) |
| voice fillers | mm lets go e4 | supported (test sw004) |
| politeness | could you play e four please | supported (test sw005) |
| word order | pawn to e4 | supported (test sw006) |
| spoken | e two to e four | supported (test sw007) |
| abbreviations | b1 to c3 pls | supported (test sw008) |
| the square | knight to the f3 square | supported (test sw009) |
| file pawn | e pawn to e4 | supported (test sw010) |
| statement-as-command | my move is d4 | supported (test sw011) |
| bare square with a question mark meaning "what is on it" | h8? | unsupported: a bare square is a move (priority 13); the question mark is not visible to the rules |
| direction words ("pawn forward", "advance the e pawn") | move the pawn forward | unsupported: no target square: a direction is not enough to select one move |

## can

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Can I move my knight to f3? | supported (test sw012) |
| wish | may i play queen h5 | supported (test sw013) |
| question | queen to h5 allowed? | supported (test sw014) |
| indirect | is h5 possible for my queen | supported (test sw015) |
| indirect | would queen to h5 be a legal move | supported (test sw016) |
| trailing "ok" ("queen h5 ok?") | queen h5 ok? | unsupported: the formalizer strips trailing "ok"/"okay" as a filler before matching, so it reads as the move |

## moves

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | What can my knight do? | supported (test sw017) |
| politeness | can u list the legal moves of the queen | supported (test sw018) |
| question | could you show what squares my queen can reach | supported (test sw019) |
| word order | my queen where can she move | supported (test sw020) |
| square | knight g1 moves? | supported (test sw021) |
| square | where can the g1 knight go | supported (test sw022) |
| square | g1 knight options | supported (test sw023) |
| square | the knight on g one, where can it go | supported (test sw024) |

## turn

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| state question | my colour? | supported (test sw025) |
| state question | am I white or black | supported (test sw026) |
| state question | are my pieces white | supported (test sw027) |
| state question | what colour are my pieces in this game | supported (test sw028) |

## side

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | switch colours with you | supported (test sw029) |
| wish | I want the other colour now | supported (test sw030) |
| voice fillers | can we swap, you take my side | supported (test sw031) |
| elliptic | black please, new game | supported (test sw032) |

## flip

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Flip the board. | supported (test sw033) |
| politeness | can u rotate the chess board | supported (test sw034) |
| indirect | show it from the other side | supported (test sw035) |
| wish | i want to see from black side | supported (test sw036) |
| indirect | turn it so i see the black side | supported (test sw037) |

## describe

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Describe the board. | supported (test sw038) |
| imperative | describe white | supported (test sw039) |
| imperative | read out the black pieces | supported (test sw040) |
| question | what white has on the board | supported (test sw041) |
| word order | white pieces please, describe | supported (test sw042) |

## where

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Where is my king? | supported (test sw043) |
| abbreviations | where r my rooks | supported (test sw044) |
| word order | rooks where? | supported (test sw045) |
| indirect | location of my rook pieces | supported (test sw046) |
| politeness | can you tell me where my two rooks are | supported (test sw047) |

## square

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | what is on e4 | supported (test sw048) |
| question | h8 has what | supported (test sw049) |

## history

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Show the move list. | supported (test sw050) |
| elliptic | move list | supported (test sw051) |
| elliptic | history of moves | supported (test sw052) |
| elliptic | moves played till now | supported (test sw053) |
| imperative | game moves please | supported (test sw054) |

## level

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Set the level to 5. | supported (test sw055) |
| wish | make it level 5 for me | supported (test sw056) |
| indirect | make the engine stronger, level five | supported (test sw057) |

## hint

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | What should I play? | supported (test sw058) |
| bare "hint" / "help" | hint please | unsupported: ui.shell game control (ui.hint, executed as chess.hint); bare "help" belongs to ui.help |

## status

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Who is winning? | supported (test sw059) |

## check

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Am I in check? | supported (test sw060) |

## last

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | What was your last move? | supported (test sw061) |

## draw

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | offer a draw | supported (test sw062) |

## new

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bare "new game" / "start over" | new game | unsupported: ui.shell game control (ui.newGame, executed as chess.new) |

## resign

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "I give up", "quit" | I give up | unsupported: ui.shell game control wins by priority (ui.giveUp, executed as chess.resign); chess patterns cover "I resign", "you win" |

## count

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| piece counts with synonyms of owners | count my pieces | unsupported: owners are kept as typed (my, you, u); the generic gold form (who=i) is not derivable |

## undo

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| negation ("do not move there") | no, not that | unsupported: a refusal of the last move needs the engine to ask something first |

files.coverage.md:
# games.guess: request-shape coverage

The system asks yes/no questions about the animal the user thinks of; the user answers, reveals the animal, or asks about the game.

Every line is either supported (with the example that has a test in `tests.sop`, ids `sw###`) or unsupported with the reason. Shapes: imperative, question, wish, indirect, statement-as-command, elliptic, voice/fillers, typos/abbreviations, word order, synonyms, references, quantities, negation/undo, coordination, politeness, state questions, option questions.

## answer

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| elliptic | yep | supported (test sw001) |
| voice fillers | um yeah it does | supported (test sw002) |
| statement-as-command | that is right | supported (test sw003) |
| abbreviations | ya | supported (test sw004) |
| synonyms | absolutely | supported (test sw005) |
| elliptic | nope | supported (test sw006) |
| typos/abbreviations | nop | supported (test sw007) |
| negation | no it isnt | supported (test sw008) |
| statement-as-command | no, thats wrong | supported (test sw009) |
| synonyms | not at all | supported (test sw010) |
| state | i dont know | supported (test sw011) |
| voice fillers | i really dont know | supported (test sw012) |
| voice fillers | sorry, i dont know the answer | supported (test sw013) |
| synonyms | no idea | supported (test sw014) |
| abbreviations | dunno | supported (test sw015) |
| synonyms | its possible | supported (test sw016) |
| elliptic | sometimes | supported (test sw017) |
| synonyms | sort of | supported (test sw018) |
| qualified answers ("yes, but only on Sundays") | Yes, but only on Sundays. | unsupported: covered by the existing qualified patterns (answer maybe) |
| number guesses / "higher" | higher | unsupported: this world is the animal game: there is no number to guess |

## start

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| statement-as-command | I have an animal in mind. | supported (test sw019) |
| imperative | Guess my animal. | supported (test sw020) |
| imperative | start twenty questions | supported (test sw021) |
| wish | ok lets play 20 questions | supported (test sw022) |
| imperative | begin the guess game pls | supported (test sw023) |
| imperative | you can start asking now | supported (test sw024) |
| imperative | start guessing | supported (test sw025) |
| wish | let's do the animal game | supported (test sw026) |
| voice fillers | time to guess, start | supported (test sw027) |
| imperative | ask me questions | supported (test sw028) |
| bare "new game" / "start over" / "play again" | new game | unsupported: ui.shell game control (ui.newGame, executed as guess.start) |
| tab words routed to ui.shell (playGame) | go ahead and start | unsupported: ambiguous with tic-tac-toe "who starts"; only resolved by the active tab (engine routing) |

## reveal

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| statement | It was a penguin. | supported (test sw029) |
| statement | it was a penguin, i had one in mind | supported (test sw030) |
| word order | the one i picked was a penguin | supported (test sw031) |
| statement | it was a penguin, add it | supported (test sw032) |
| elliptic | a penguin, new animal for you | supported (test sw033) |
| noisy gold with an extra avatar action ("you got it wrong, it was a tiger") | you got it wrong, it was a tiger | unsupported: the first clause is an accusation, not a command; the reveal is still parsed |

## why

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Why did you ask that? | supported (test sw034) |
| question | why is that question being asked | supported (test sw035) |
| question | what made you pick that question | supported (test sw036) |
| question | why did you choose it | supported (test sw037) |

## remaining

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Which animals are left? | supported (test sw038) |
| question | what can it still be | supported (test sw039) |
| imperative | list what it could be | supported (test sw040) |
| elliptic | possible ones now? | supported (test sw041) |
| question | which are left in the list | supported (test sw042) |

## count

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | How many questions have you asked? | supported (test sw043) |
| question | how many questions are you on | supported (test sw044) |

## repeat

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Repeat the question. | supported (test sw045) |
| politeness | could you repeat your question | supported (test sw046) |
| voice fillers | sorry, say that again | supported (test sw047) |
| statement | i missed it, again? | supported (test sw048) |

## giveup

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| statement | I give up. | supported (test sw049) |

## hint

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| asking for a hint | give me a hint | unsupported: the system is the guesser: guess.hint only explains that it gives no hints (ui.shell hint control) |

files.coverage.md:
# games.hangman: request-shape coverage

The system hides an animal word; the user guesses letters or the whole word, asks for facts and for the masked word, starts or gives up.

Every line is either supported (with the example that has a test in `tests.sop`, ids `sw###`) or unsupported with the reason. Shapes: imperative, question, wish, indirect, statement-as-command, elliptic, voice/fillers, typos/abbreviations, word order, synonyms, references, quantities, negation/undo, coordination, politeness, state questions, option questions.

## letter

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Is there an E? | supported (test sw001) |
| question | o is there? | supported (test sw002) |
| question | is it n | supported (test sw003) |
| elliptic | L | supported (test sw004) |
| voice fillers | um, next letter, n | supported (test sw005) |
| spoken name | zed | supported (test sw006) |
| question | does z appear | supported (test sw007) |
| statement | guessing z | supported (test sw008) |
| wish | can i get an r | supported (test sw009) |
| question | any e? | supported (test sw010) |
| imperative | try the letter s | supported (test sw011) |
| word order | e in the word? | supported (test sw012) |
| abbreviations | got any s pls | supported (test sw013) |
| spoken name | try double you | supported (test sw014) |
| undo / take back a letter | undo that letter | unsupported: a guessed letter cannot be taken back in hangman |
| several letters in one message | e and a | unsupported: one letter per request; the dispatcher splits coordinated messages into pieces |

## word

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Is it tiger? | supported (test sw015) |
| elliptic | tiger? | supported (test sw016) |
| statement | tiger, my answer | supported (test sw017) |
| question | is tiger right | supported (test sw018) |
| statement | my final answer is tiger | supported (test sw019) |
| imperative | I guess tiger | supported (test sw020) |
| multi-word animals ("polar bear") | is it a polar bear | unsupported: only single-word animals are hangman words |

## hint

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Tell me something about it. | supported (test sw021) |
| imperative | tell me a fact about it | supported (test sw022) |
| elliptic | fact? | supported (test sw023) |
| wish | i want a fact | supported (test sw024) |
| question | what is it known for | supported (test sw025) |
| imperative | tell me one thing about this animal | supported (test sw026) |
| voice fillers | uh give me something about it, not a letter | supported (test sw027) |
| question | whats a fact about the mystery animal | supported (test sw028) |
| bare "hint" | hint please | unsupported: ui.shell game control (ui.hint, executed as hm.hint) |

## status

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | How many guesses are left? | supported (test sw029) |
| question | how many letters are hidden | supported (test sw030) |
| question | what does the word look like now | supported (test sw031) |
| imperative | show me the mask | supported (test sw032) |
| imperative | display the dashes | supported (test sw033) |
| elliptic | letters still missing? | supported (test sw034) |
| question | how many spaces left in the word | supported (test sw035) |
| elliptic | hidden word view | supported (test sw036) |

## new

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Start a new hangman game. | supported (test sw037) |
| elliptic | hangman again | supported (test sw038) |
| voice fillers | play again hangman | supported (test sw039) |
| word order | hangman round two | supported (test sw040) |
| wish | lets go again with a new animal | supported (test sw041) |
| imperative | start over hangman | supported (test sw042) |
| statement | giraffe is the word | supported (test sw043) |
| imperative | make a hangman round with giraffe pls | supported (test sw044) |
| word order | hidden word: giraffe | supported (test sw045) |
| imperative | ok new hangman, its giraffe | supported (test sw046) |
| politeness | can u set the word to giraffe for hangman | supported (test sw047) |
| imperative | Play hangman with the word zebra. | supported (test sw048) |
| bare "new game" / "new game pls" / "start over" | new game pls | unsupported: ui.shell game control (ui.newGame, executed as hm.new) |

## giveup

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| statement | I give up the word. | supported (test sw049) |
| imperative | end the game pls | supported (test sw050) |
| "I give up", "I quit", "forget it" | I give up | unsupported: ui.shell game control wins by priority and runs hm.giveup; the hangman patterns cover the longer forms |

files.coverage.md:
# games.tictactoe: request-shape coverage

The board is 3x3; the user is X (moves first unless asked), the system is O.

Every line is either supported (with the example that has a test in `tests.sop`, ids `sw###`) or unsupported with the reason. Shapes: imperative, question, wish, indirect, statement-as-command, elliptic, voice/fillers, typos/abbreviations, word order, synonyms, references, quantities, negation/undo, coordination, politeness, state questions, option questions.

## move

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Play the center. | supported (test sw001) |
| wish | I would like the top left corner please. | supported (test sw002) |
| question | Can I go bottom right? | supported (test sw003) |
| elliptic | top right | supported (test sw004) |
| voice fillers | um, top right I think | supported (test sw005) |
| voice fillers | uh okay gonna take the middle left | supported (test sw006) |
| abbreviations | bl pls | supported (test sw007) |
| word order | the left side of the middle row | supported (test sw008) |
| word order | middle of the bottom row | supported (test sw009) |
| synonyms | the one at the bottom in the middle | supported (test sw010) |
| synonyms | bot middle | supported (test sw011) |
| synonyms | down the bottom, middle column | supported (test sw012) |
| statement-as-command | my move is the center | supported (test sw013) |
| politeness | hey could you put my x in the top middle please | supported (test sw014) |
| coordinate | B2 | supported (test sw015) |
| coordinate | square c3 for me | supported (test sw016) |
| coordinate | gonna take c3 | supported (test sw017) |
| spoken coordinate | bee two pls | supported (test sw018) |
| number words | row two column three | supported (test sw019) |
| quantities | 3 1 | supported (test sw020) |
| ordinals | second row third column | supported (test sw021) |
| ordinals | third row, left-most square | supported (test sw022) |
| pronoun/reference ("the same one", "there") | put it there again | unsupported: no reference target: the board has no focus object |
| undo / take back a mark | undo my move | unsupported: no undo operation in this world |
| coordination of two moves | center then top left | unsupported: a move is answered by the system move in the same turn; only the first mark is taken per sentence |

## new

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Start a new tic tac toe game. | supported (test sw023) |
| imperative | Clear the board. | supported (test sw024) |
| wish | I want a fresh game | supported (test sw025) |
| elliptic | clean board | supported (test sw026) |
| voice fillers | um play again from scratch | supported (test sw027) |
| synonyms | lets start over from the beginning | supported (test sw028) |
| bare "new game" / "start over" in the tic-tac-toe tab | new game | unsupported: handled by the ui.shell game control (ui.newGame, executed as ttt.new); a world-level pattern would steal "new game" from the other games and the shell outside the tab (engine routing) |

## first

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Let me go 1st | supported (test sw029) |
| question | can I start? | supported (test sw030) |
| imperative | You go first. | supported (test sw031) |
| wish | I want you to start | supported (test sw032) |
| choosing a mark ("I am x and I start") | I am x and I start | unsupported: the mark is fixed (user X, system O); no operation to choose a mark |

## whoFirst

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Who goes first? | supported (test sw033) |
| abbreviations | whos up first | supported (test sw034) |

## status

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | Who is winning? | supported (test sw035) |
| elliptic | winning? | supported (test sw036) |
| abbreviations | whos winning rn | supported (test sw037) |

## describe

| Shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imperative | Describe the board. | supported (test sw038) |

# geo.map coverage catalogue (R2)

For every operation of the map world, the request shapes a user may use. `supported` lines are matched by general patterns in `patterns.sop` (the generated block `pat.geo.map.w.*` plus the base patterns) and have a test in `tests.sop` (`t.geo.map.r2nNNN`, text = start of the reply). `unsupported` lines say why.

Shape classes considered: imperative, question, wish, indirect, statement-as-command, elliptic, voice style (fillers, run-ons), typos and abbreviations (u, r, pls, thx, whats), word-order variants, synonyms, pronouns and references, quantities/units/number words, negation and undo, coordination, politeness, questions about state, questions about options.

Cross-cutting support (all operations): sentence-initial and trailing fillers and chat words (uh, um, hmm, like, hey so, pls, plz, thx, lol, real quick, buddy), polite and wish frames (can u, could you, I wanna, I need to know, do you know, tell me, quick question), commas, number words (digits after normalisation), `whats`, `r`/`u`, `n` for "and", `'s` and bare possessives (japans, romanias), demonym adjectives (japanese, brazilian, romanian ... via `lex.geo.map.demonyms`, resolved to the country in ops.mjs), typo correction by the engine (when a unique known word is within distance), and sequential coordination ("show Paris, then zoom in") through clause splitting.

files.data/README.md:
# Data of the world geo.map

All files here and the knowledge base (`kb.sop`) and place lexicon (`lexicon.sop`) are generated by `scripts/build-geo-data.mjs` from npm packages. Do not edit them by hand.

| Data | Package (version) | Licence | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Countries: names, capitals, region, borders, area, currencies, languages, landlocked | world-countries 5.1.0 (mledoze/countries) | ODbL 1.0 (attribution and share-alike for the database) | `geo.map.country` wires |
| Country population | country-json 2.3.0 (country-by-population, about 2018 estimates) | MIT | `pop` of countries (Timor-Leste added by hand: World Bank 2018) |
| Cities | all-the-cities 3.1.0 (GeoNames gazetteer, https://www.geonames.org) | CC BY 4.0 (attribution required) | `geo.map.city` wires: 246 capitals, every city of 500,000+ people, Romanian and Moldovan cities of 30,000+ (1001 in all) |
| Country outlines (offline base map) | world-atlas 2.0.2 countries-50m (Natural Earth) | public domain | `docs/webchat/vendor/map/countries-50m.json`, bounding boxes of countries (`bb`) |
| Groups (EU, NATO, Nordic ...) | hand-written, as of 2024 | none | `geo.map.region` wires of kind `group` |

Every KB wire carries its source and licence in `core.source`. Population figures are rough and dated; city populations are GeoNames city-proper values (a few large cities are much smaller than their metro areas).

Counts: 250 countries and territories (194 independent), 1001 cities, 38 regions, 1464 lexicon names. Capitals without a GeoNames match (no city wire; the capital name is still known): EH:El Aaiún, IO:Diego Garcia, TK:Fakaofo.

Rebuild: `npm i world-countries@5.1.0 all-the-cities@3.1.0 country-json@2.3.0 world-atlas@2.0.2 topojson-client@3.1.0` in a temporary directory, then `node scripts/build-geo-data.mjs --modules <dir>/node_modules`.

files.coverage.md:
# kids.animals: request-shape catalogue (R2)

Status: **S** = supported by general patterns, with tests in `tests.sop` (`t.animals.*`; `s###` come from the rule sweep); **U** = unsupported, with the reason.
Operations: questions on one animal (legs, food, class, abilities, sound, baby, covering, habitat, summary, yes/no on class or diet), searches over the KB (by legs, habitat, class, diet, ability, food, sound, covering), the reverse baby question (what is a calf), pets (tell a pet and its name, ask for it), and teaching facts.

Shared shape rules (apply to every question below): politeness and lead-ins (`can you tell me`, `can u say`, `remind me`, `pls`, `hey`, `quick question`, `i wonder`), tails (`pls`, `thanks`, `lol`, `btw`, `real quick`), plurals and `a/an/the/every/any/all`, number words for numbers, kid typos of animal names (`pengiun`, `rabit`, `elefant`, ... in `lexicon.sop`) and of abilities (`flyy`, `swimm`), synonyms `kitty`, `doggy`, `mallard`.

## legs of one animal
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | how many legs does a spider have / has a spider got / do spiders have, how many feet does a dog have | S |
| prepositional | how many legs on a spider, legs on a spider, number of legs of a dog, tell me the legs of a spider | S |
| noun first / elliptic | spider legs?, spider leg number, spiders how many legs pls, dog legs how many, count spider legs | S |
| imperative / wish | tell me how many legs a spider has, can you say how many legs a spider has | S |
| yes/no with a number | does a dog have 4 legs, is it true that a spider has eight legs, a spider has 8 legs right | S |
| statement as teaching | a spider has 8 legs, remember a zebra has 4 legs, fyi zebra 4 legs, a zebra got 4 legs | S |

## food of one animal
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | what does a rabbit eat, what do rabbits eat, what food does a rabbit need | S |
| synonyms of "eat" | like to eat, munch on, live on, feed on, dine on, usually eat, is eating | S |
| noun first / elliptic | rabbit food?, rabbit diet pls, rabbits eat what | S |
| about the diet | what is the diet of a cow, what is a lion's favorite food | S |
| yes/no | does a rabbit eat carrots, cows eat meat right? | S |
| plant / meat eater yes/no | does a cow eat plants, is a cow a plant eater, is a lion a meat eater, does a bear eat both meat and plants | S (read as the diet class: herbivore, carnivore, omnivore) |
| teaching | rabbits eat carrots, a rabbit eats carrots and grass | S |

## class, diet and kind (yes/no)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| aux question | is a whale a fish, are bats mammals | S |
| tag question | a bat is a bird right?, whales are fish true? | S |
| lead-ins | is it true a whale is a fish, would a dolphin count as a mammal, u think a dolphin's a mammal, would you call a cow a carnivore | S |
| adjectives | is a cow carnivorous / herbivorous / vegetarian | S |
| one-or-the-other | is a whale a fish or a mammal | S (answers for the first kind named) |
| what kind of animal | what kind of animal is a whale, what type of animal is a frog | S |
| teaching | a whale is a mammal, a lion is a carnivore | S |

## abilities (fly, swim)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | can a penguin fly, do penguins fly, is a whale able to swim | S |
| synonyms | take off, flap, soar, glide; go in water, float, paddle, dive; good at swimming, good swimmers | S |
| noun first / elliptic | penguin fly?, bunny swim or no | S |
| lead-ins | can u tell me if a cat can swim, is it possible for a penguin to fly, is it true a bat can fly, do you think a dolphin can swim | S |
| typos | can pengiun fly, can penguins flyy | S |
| teaching | a duck can swim, a penguin cannot fly, zebras dont swim, a zebra cant swim, a zebra is not able to swim | S |
| other abilities (run, climb, jump) | | U: the legend has only `can_fly` and `can_swim` |

## sound, baby, covering, habitat, summary
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sound | what sound does a cow make, what does a cow say, cow sound?, cow say?, tell me the sound a cow makes, cows say what | S |
| baby | what is a baby cow called, baby cow name?, cow baby?, what do you call the baby of a cow, whats a baby sheep called | S |
| baby reverse | what is a calf, whats a calf, calf?, calf meaning, tell me about calves, who is a calf, puppy is the baby of what | S |
| covering | what is a duck covered in, what covers a cow's body, whats a cow covered in, cow skin is covered in what, what is the covering of a cow, what kind of skin or fur does a cow have, covering of a duck? | S |
| habitat | where does a camel live, where can i find a camel, where is a camel's home, camel home?, camels where pls, where would i meet a camel | S |
| summary | tell me about the lion, what is a lion like, whats a dolphin like, dolphins tell me, dolphin info pls, give me the basics on dolphins, whats the deal with dolphins | S |
| questions about a trait not in the KB (friendly, smart, how big, how old) | are dolphins friendly | U: no key in the legend |

## searches
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| by legs | animals with six legs, 6 legs animals, six legged animals?, which animals got 6 legs, animals with no legs, animals without legs | S |
| by habitat (with synonyms) | which animals live in the sea / ocean, sea animals, what lives in the ocean, name the sea animals, what creatures live in the sea, animals of the ocean pls, jungle/rainforest, polar/arctic, woods, farm/barn, garden/backyard ... | S |
| by class / diet | name a bird, list all reptiles, give me some mammals, which animals are carnivores | S |
| by ability, with class | which animals can fly, animals that cannot swim, which animals cant swim, flying animals, swimming bird please, a bird that swims name one, name a bird which swims well, tell me a bird that is good at swimming | S |
| by food / sound / covering | which animals eat grass, which animals say moo, which animals have feathers | S |

## pets
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tell | my dog is called Rex, the dog is named rex, my dogs name is rex, rex is my dog, rex is the name of my dog, name of my dog: rex, i have a dog called rex, i named my dog Rex, my doggy is rex, my pet cat is called tom, i have a cat and its called tom | S (lowercase names work for the typical pet names in `lexicon.sop`; any capitalized word is a name) |
| ask for the name | what is my dog called, whats my pets name, my pet name?, what did i call my pet, name of my pet?, remind me my pets name, can you tell me what my pet is called | S (a specific kind keeps `where.kind`, "pet" asks without kind) |
| ask what pets | which pets do i have, do i have a dog, who is Rex, what pet is Rex, is Rex a dog | S |
| two clauses with a comma ("ive got a cat, her name is tom", "meet tom, hes my cat") | | U: a clause cut at the comma has no animal in the second half |

## Cross-cutting
| Shape | Status |
| --- | --- |
| wish ("i want to know ...") and indirect forms | S (lead-ins) |
| voice fillers, run-ons | S (`um`, `like`, `so`, `ok`, double lead-ins) |
| pronouns ("it", "they" for the animal just asked about) | U: the rule formalizer has no animal coreference; only pets read the session |
| negation | `a snake has no legs`, `dogs dont eat pizza` are not facts to teach (negative tests in `datagen.mjs`) |
| coordination | "a rabbit eats carrots and grass" S |
| questions about the state ("what do you know") / options | answered by `ui.help` |
| spelling of the animal | S for the listed typos; unknown typos are read as a new animal name |

@legend.kids.animals core.legend
    namespace=kids.animals
    version=0.1.0
    imports=core
    imports=kids.common
    doc="Animals and their properties, and the pets a child tells about"

@kids.animals.animal core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Facts about one kind of animal. Several wires may describe the same kind (knowledge base and things taught in the dialog); their keys are merged."
    example="A spider has 8 legs."
    example="Zebras eat grass."
    negative="Tom has 8 apples."

@kids.animals.animal.name core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which kind of animal is it?"

@kids.animals.animal.class core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which class is it (mammal, bird, fish, insect, reptile, amphibian, arachnid ...)?"

@kids.animals.animal.legs core.key
    value=integer
    ask="How many legs does it have?"

@kids.animals.animal.diet core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Is it a herbivore, a carnivore or an omnivore?"

@kids.animals.animal.food core.key
    value=string
    ask="What does it eat?"
    card=many

@kids.animals.animal.habitat core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Where does it live (farm, forest, sea, river, jungle, desert, polar, home ...)?"
    card=many

@kids.animals.animal.covering core.key
    value=atom
    ask="What covers its body (fur, feather, scale, skin, shell ...)?"
    card=many

@kids.animals.animal.sound core.key
    value=string
    ask="Which sound does it make?"

@kids.animals.animal.baby core.key
    value=atom
    ask="What is its baby called?"

@kids.animals.animal.can_fly core.key
    value=boolean
    ask="Can it fly?"
    compute=true

@kids.animals.animal.can_swim core.key
    value=boolean
    ask="Can it swim?"
    compute=true

@kids.animals.animal.is_a core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which class or diet is asked about (for yes/no questions)?"
    compute=true
    observe=false

@kids.animals.animal.lives core.key
    value=string
    ask="Where does it live?"
    compute=true
    observe=false

@kids.animals.animal.covered core.key
    value=string
    ask="What is its body covered in?"
    compute=true
    observe=false

@kids.animals.animal.summary core.key
    value=string
    ask="What is it like?"
    compute=true
    observe=false

@kids.animals.animal.matching core.key
    value=string
    ask="Which animals match the given properties?"
    card=many
    compute=true
    observe=false

    ask="What is the pet called?"

files.operations.sop:
@op.kids.animals.canFlyYes core.operation
    outputs=kids.animals.animal.can_fly
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.name
    impl=canFlyYes
    semantics=query
    doc="Yes when some statement says the animal can fly; conflicting when statements disagree; missing when nothing is stated."

@op.kids.animals.canFlyNo core.operation
    outputs=kids.animals.animal.can_fly
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.name
    impl=canFlyNo
    semantics=query
    doc="No only when a statement explicitly says the animal cannot fly (refuted); otherwise missing (unknown)."

@op.kids.animals.canSwimYes core.operation
    outputs=kids.animals.animal.can_swim
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.name
    impl=canSwimYes
    semantics=query
    doc="Yes when some statement says the animal can swim."

@op.kids.animals.canSwimNo core.operation
    outputs=kids.animals.animal.can_swim
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.name
    impl=canSwimNo
    semantics=query
    doc="No only when a statement explicitly says the animal cannot swim."

@op.kids.animals.isAYes core.operation
    outputs=kids.animals.animal.is_a
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.name
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.is_a
    impl=isAYes
    semantics=query
    doc="Yes when the animal has the asked class or diet; conflicting when several classes are stated."

@op.kids.animals.isANo core.operation
    outputs=kids.animals.animal.is_a
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.name
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.is_a
    impl=isANo
    semantics=query
    doc="No, with the actual class or diet, when the animal is known to have another one."

@op.kids.animals.livesWhere core.operation
    outputs=kids.animals.animal.lives
    inputs=kids.animals.animal.name
    impl=livesWhere
    semantics=query
    doc="A phrase telling where the animal lives, from all its habitats."

    impl=coveredIn

    doc="A short description from class, habitat, legs, covering, food and abilities."

files.coverage.md:
# kids.arith — request-shape catalogue (rule formalizer)

Status: **S** = supported, with a test in `tests.sop` (the `doc=` text of the `t.arith.swNNN` tests is the class name used below); **U** = unsupported, with the reason.
All patterns are in `patterns.sop` (older families first, the rule-sweep families `sw.*` last); fillers, politeness and chat abbreviations come from the shared prefix/suffix alternations (`uh`, `um`, `hey`, `can u`, `pls`, `thx`, `rn`, ...).

## Statements (state changes)
| Operation | Request shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| holding | plain / "has got" / "now" | Tom has 5 apples. | S (older tests n1-n25) |
| holding | modifiers, possessive, noun-first, belongs-to | Ana is holding 4 pears. / Ana's got 4 pears. / 4 pears belong to Ana. / FYI Ana has 4 pears left. | S: "statement: have with modifiers" |
| holding | none / negation | Ben has zero pears. / Ben doesn't have any pears. / Ben ran out of pears. | S: "statement: has none" |
| holding | user as owner, number words | I have five marbles. | S (n13, n15, number-word tests) |
| buy | verb synonyms, fillers, tails, passive, "from the shop" | Zoe just bought 5 pencils. / 5 pencils were bought by Zoe. / Zoe got 5 pencils from the shop. | S: "statement: buy ..." |
| eat, lose, break, receive | verb synonyms, perfect tense, passive, tails (today/yesterday/now), "a/an" | Tom has just eaten 3 apples. / 3 apples were lost by Tom. / Amy has just found 4 shells. | S: "statement: eat/lose/..." |
| give | direct / "to" / "from" / "of his", verbs hand/pass/send | Ana gives Tom 3 pears. | S (older tests) |
| all change verbs | ellipsis and pronouns ("He ate 2.") | Tom has 9 apples. He ate 3. | S (older tests n11, n20) |
| any | two statements in one sentence | Tom has 5 apples and Ana has 4. | S (older); long run-ons are the dispatcher's job |

## Questions
| Operation | Request shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count (holding) | standard | How many apples does Tom have? | S (n3) |
| count | noun-first, fillers, "is at", number-of, possessive count, after-event, ellipsis of the item | Leo stickers how many / Uh Leo has how many stickers / How many stickers is Leo at now / What is Leo's sticker number | S: "holding question ..." |
| count | typo ("hs", "hass", "stikers") | mia hs 7 marbles | S via the typo corrector when the sentence is otherwise known; otherwise U (engine typo budget, three words per sentence) |
| has | do/does/has, "any ... for X", "is there ... with X", "do u know if", "still" | Any pears for Ben? / Do u know if Ben has pears? | S: "has-any question" |
| total (everybody) | altogether / in total / whole group / sum of everybody's / add all up | All the stickers total? / Add all the stickers up for me. | S: "total of everybody" |
| total (two people) | together / between / sum of A and B's / noun-first / "A + B" | Total marbles for Leo and Zoe. / Marbles Leo + Zoe? | S: "total of two people" |
| leader | who has the most / highest / biggest pile / person with the most / whose X are the most | Who has the highest number of stickers? | S: "who has the most" |
| leader (pair) | who has more A or B, "A or B more X?", "more X: A or B", "A vs B who wins", "between A and B who has more", "who is ahead on X" | Whos got more marbles, Leo or Zoe? | S: "who has more between two" (order of the pair follows the sentence) |
| gap | how many more/fewer, difference, lack, behind, short, "how far behind", "compared to" | How many marbles does Zoe lack compared to Leo? | S: "gap ..." |
| verdict | does A have more than B / beat / ahead of / "A has more than B, right?" | Does Lily beat Sam in stickers? | S: "verdict ..." |
| any question | no number or item | Who has more apples? | S as "unparsed": n5 (the world asks for the numbers) |

## Arithmetic
| Operation | Request shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| calc plus/minus/times/divide | symbol and word forms, "whats", "can u do", "calc", "for me", "is?", "equals what", words for numbers | Whats 15 minus 8 / 15 less 8 is? / 6 x 7 pls / 20 div 4 | S: "calc: ..." |
| calc | "N more/less than M", "N from M", "add N and M for me" | What is 5 more than 7? / What is 8 from 15? | S |
| divide | sharing story | If I share 20 among 4 how many each? | S |
| double / half | doubling, doubled, "give me double", halve, "in half", "half of" | Could u halve 12 for me | S: "calc: double and half" / "calc: half" ("give me double 13" loses to ui.avatar, see below) |

## Not supported
* `+`/`-` next to a word (`7 +5` is fine, `march + 4` is dropped by the tokenizer): engine, `src/formalizer/rules/normalize.mjs`.
* possessives without an apostrophe ("leos marbles", "zoes marbles"): the `agent` class needs an apostrophe form; engine.
* mis-spelled number words ("fourty"): `src/formalizer/rules/numbers.mjs`.
* "Tom vs Ana, how many more apples for Tom?" and "how many less marbles does zoe have": the second person is implicit; needs a reference to the last pair of agents.
* "give me double 13" in no-tab sessions: `ui.avatar` (`give me ...`) outranks it by priority; routing, not rules.
* a statement and a question in one run-on sentence ("tom got 5 apples and ana gave him 3 more, how many apples does tom have now"): dispatcher splitting.
* more than two people in "total" / "who has more".

    doc="Someone has a number of items of one kind. A statement sets the count; later events change it."
    example="Tom has 5 apples."
    negative="Tom likes apples."

@kids.arith.holding.owner core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who has them?"

@kids.arith.holding.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.holding.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many are there?"
    observe=true
    compute=true

@kids.arith.change core.type
    extends=core.event
    doc="Something happens to the number of items someone has. Events are applied in dialog order (core.seq)."
    example="Ana gives Tom 3 apples."

@kids.arith.change.who core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is it about (who gives, gets, eats, loses, buys or breaks)?"

@kids.arith.change.to core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who receives the items?"

@kids.arith.change.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.change.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many items are involved?"

@kids.arith.give core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="One person gives some items to another person: who gives, to receives."
    example="Ana gives Tom 3 apples."

@kids.arith.receive core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone gets, receives or finds some items."
    example="Tom finds 2 marbles."

@kids.arith.eat core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone eats some items."
    example="Tom ate 2 apples."

@kids.arith.lose core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone loses some items."
    example="Mia lost 3 marbles."

@kids.arith.buy core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone buys some items (only the counts are tracked here, not the money)."
    example="Ben buys 4 pencils."

@kids.arith.break core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone breaks some items."
    example="Sam broke 2 pencils."

@kids.arith.total core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="How many items of one kind there are altogether, over everybody or over two named people."
    example="How many apples are there altogether?"

@kids.arith.total.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.total.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person to count?"

@kids.arith.total.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person to count?"

@kids.arith.total.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many are there altogether?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.leader core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Who has the most items of one kind, or who of two named people has more."
    example="Who has more apples, Tom or Ana?"

@kids.arith.leader.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.leader.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person to compare?"

@kids.arith.leader.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person to compare?"

@kids.arith.leader.winner core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who has more?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.gap core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="How many more (or fewer) items of one kind the first person has than the second."
    example="How many more apples does Tom have than Ana?"

@kids.arith.gap.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.gap.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person?"

@kids.arith.gap.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person?"

@kids.arith.gap.diff core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the difference between the two counts?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.verdict core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Yes or no: does the first person have more items than the second?"
    example="Does Tom have more apples than Ana?"

@kids.arith.verdict.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.verdict.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person?"

@kids.arith.verdict.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person?"

@kids.arith.verdict.answer core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Is it yes or no?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.has core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Yes or no: does someone have any items of one kind?"
    example="Does Tom have any apples?"

@kids.arith.has.owner core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who might have them?"

@kids.arith.has.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.has.answer core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Is it yes or no?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.calc core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A bare calculation of two numbers: plus, minus, times, divided_by."
    example="What is 7 plus 5?"

@kids.arith.calc.op core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which operation (plus, minus, times, divided_by)?"

@kids.arith.calc.a core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the first number?"

@kids.arith.calc.b core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the second number?"

@kids.arith.calc.result core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the result?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.half core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Half of a number."
    example="What is half of 10?"

@kids.arith.half.n core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="Which number?"

@kids.arith.half.result core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is half of it?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.double core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Double a number."
    example="What is double 6?"

@kids.arith.double.n core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="Which number?"

@kids.arith.double.result core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is double it?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.calc.op2 core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which second operation (plus, minus, times, divided_by)?"

@kids.arith.calc.c core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the third number?"
