files.operations.sop:
@op.kids.arith.currentCount core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.holding.count
    inputs=kids.arith.holding.owner
    inputs=kids.arith.holding.item
    impl=currentCount
    semantics=query
    doc="The number someone has after applying, in dialog order, every statement of having and every giving, getting, eating, losing, buying and breaking. A person whose starting count is unknown stays unknown; an impossible event gives a conflict."

@op.kids.arith.totalCount core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.total.count
    inputs=kids.arith.total.item
    inputs=kids.arith.total.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.total.who2
    impl=totalCount
    semantics=query
    doc="The sum of the counts of everybody whose count is known (or of two named people)."

@op.kids.arith.leader core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.leader.winner
    inputs=kids.arith.leader.item
    inputs=kids.arith.leader.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.leader.who2
    impl=leader
    semantics=query
    doc="Who has the most (or more, between two people). A tie is ambiguous."

@op.kids.arith.gap core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.gap.diff
    inputs=kids.arith.gap.item
    inputs=kids.arith.gap.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.gap.who2
    impl=gap
    semantics=query
    doc="How many more or fewer items the first person has than the second."

@op.kids.arith.verdict core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.verdict.answer
    inputs=kids.arith.verdict.item
    inputs=kids.arith.verdict.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.verdict.who2
    impl=verdict
    semantics=query
    doc="Yes or no: does the first person have more than the second?"

@op.kids.arith.hasAny core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.has.answer
    inputs=kids.arith.has.owner
    inputs=kids.arith.has.item
    impl=hasAny
    semantics=query
    doc="Yes or no: does the person have at least one item of the kind?"

@op.kids.arith.calc core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.calc.result
    inputs=kids.arith.calc.op
    inputs=kids.arith.calc.a
    inputs=kids.arith.calc.b
    inputs=kids.arith.calc.op2
    inputs=kids.arith.calc.c
    impl=calc
    semantics=compute
    doc="plus, minus, times and divided_by with exact integer or decimal results; division by zero is refused politely."

@op.kids.arith.half core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.half.result
    inputs=kids.arith.half.n
    impl=half
    semantics=compute
    doc="Half of a number."

@op.kids.arith.double core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.double.result
    inputs=kids.arith.double.n
    impl=double
    semantics=compute
    doc="Double a number."
files.patterns.sop:
@pat.kids.arith.has core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [now]? [has|have|had] [got|now]? {n:number} {item:lex.kids.arith.items} [now|left|today|at_first|at_the_start]?"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={n} item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=9
    example="Tom has 5 apples."

@pat.kids.arith.has.a core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [now]? [has|have|had] [got]? [a|an] {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count=1 item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=10
    example="Mia has a pear."

@pat.kids.arith.has.no core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [has|have|had] [got]? no {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count=0 item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=10
    example="Ben has no marbles."

@pat.kids.arith.has.start core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [starts|started|begins|began] with {n:number} {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={n} item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=10
    example="Lily starts with 8 stickers."

@pat.kids.arith.has.two core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [has|have|had] [got]? {n:number} {item:lex.kids.arith.items} and {m:number} {item2:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={n} item={item}\n@{_1} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={m} item={item2}"
    kind=statement
    priority=11
    example="Tom has 4 apples and 3 pears."

@pat.kids.arith.give.direct core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [gives|gave|give] {to:agent} {n:number} [more]? {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"

    priority=9
    example="Ana gives 3 apples to Tom."

@pat.kids.arith.give.to.a core.pattern

    kind=statement
    priority=10
    example="Ana gave an apple to Tom."

@pat.kids.arith.give.of core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [gives|gave|give] {n:number} of [his|her|their|my|the]? {item:lex.kids.arith.items} to {to:agent}"

# kids.common: request-shape catalogue (R2)

Status: **S** = supported by general patterns, with at least one test in `tests.sop` (ids `t.kids.common.*`, the ones numbered `s###` come from the rule sweep); **U** = unsupported, with the reason.
Chat acts are `core.request action=chat.<act>`; the operations are `greet`, `name`, `who`, `meet`, `myname`, `thanks`, `bye` (`ops.mjs`).

## greet (chat.greet)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bare greeting, imperative-free | hello, hi, hey, yo, hiya, howdy, heya, good morning/afternoon/evening | S |
| typos and stretched forms | hii, hiii, heyyy, helloo, helo, hllo, hallo, henlo, hewwo | S |
| with addressee | hello robot, hi bot, hey buddy, hello my friend, hi everyone, hey you | S |
| repeated | hello hello, hey hey hey, hi hi | S |
| with a small question inside | hello friend how are u, hey are you there (chat-engine pattern wins when a chess tab is open) | S (standalone "how are you" is deliberately **not** a greeting: it is a question) |
| "it is me" forms | hello again it's me, hi it is me again | S |
| politeness | hi there pls, hello please | S |
| other languages | hola, ahoy, salutations | S |

## name (assistant name, chat.name)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | what is your name, whats ur name, wat is ur name, what are you called, how are you called | S |
| imperative | tell me your name, say your name, could you say your name, give me ur name | S |
| wish / indirect | i wanna know your name, can i get your name, may i ask your name, can you tell me what your name is | S |
| elliptic | your name?, name?, ur name pls, name you go by?, name u use pls | S |
| word-order variants | your name again, name of yours, name of the helper, helper name please | S |
| synonyms of "name" | nickname, handle, first name, "what do you go by", "what do you call yourself" | S |
| other nouns for the assistant | what is the bot's name, whats the helper called, the helper is called what, what is the name of this helper, who is the name behind this chat | S |
| about how others address it | how do people call you, what do ppl call u, folks call u what, how do others know you, what should I call you, how can i call you, what do i call the assistant, how should I address u | S |
| fillers | hey, so, um, wait, yo friend, pls, plz, "quick question", "can u tell me" | S |
| who named you / who made you | (a different question, not a name request) | U (no operation) |

## who (what the assistant is, chat.who)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | who are you, who r u, what are you, who is this, who am i talking to (read as name by an older pattern) | S |
| imperative | introduce yourself, intro yourself pls, tell me about yourself, describe yourself, can u introduce urself, introduce yourself to me please | S |
| kind of thing | what kind of bot are you, which bot are you, what bot is this, what kinda bot u r, what type of bot you are | S |
| elliptic | bot type?, your identity?, intro | S |
| "are you a robot" | are you a robot / human / real | S for chat; the avatar world answers it when the avatar tab is the context |
| two questions in one comma-joined message | "tell me about you, who are u" | U (a message cut at the comma gives two requests; the dataset target has one; handled by the dispatcher's segmentation) |

## meet (the user says their name, chat.meet; remembered per session)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "my name is" family | my name is Ben, my name's Ben, name is Ben, my nickname is Ben | S |
| call-me family | call me Ben, you can call me Ben, u can call me Ben, please call me Ben, you may call me Ben | S |
| they-call family | they call me Ben, everyone calls me Ben, my friends call me Ben, people call me Ben | S |
| i-am family with a capitalized or known first name | I am Ben, Im Ben, hey im Ben, i am Mia Lee, Im Mia | S |
| name first | Ben is my name, Ben here, Ben speaking, Zed is my name pls, "Ben's my name" | S |
| with lead-ins / tails | just so you know my name is Ben, hello my name is Ben by the way, name's Ben btw, hi im Ben nice to meet you | S |
| "this is" | this is Ben, hi this is Ben talking | S |
| "Ben is fine/ok for me" | Ben works, Ben would be good | S |
| lowercase unknown names ("im zed", "i am zed") | | U for the `i am` family: a lowercase word that is not a known first name is not read as a name (it would swallow "i am hungry"); the other families accept any word. Capitalized names always work. |
| case of the stored name | the name is stored as typed in the text, then capitalized by the operation | S (the dataset targets keep the original capital, so lowercase inputs cannot match them) |
| not names | I am hungry, I am tired, I am 7 years old, Im happy | S (negative tests in `datagen.mjs`) |

## myname (what is my name, chat.myname)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | what is my name, whats my name, what was my name again, who am i, what am i called | S |
| memory question | do you remember my name, do u know my name, can you recall my name, did u learn my name yet, do you have my name saved | S |
| recognition | do you recognize me, u recognise me or not, are you able to recognise me, can you tell if you recognise me, remember me? | S |
| imperative | say my name, remind me what is my name, tell me my name, guess my name lol do you know it | S |
| about what was said | what name did i tell u earlier, what was the name i said, remind me which name i told you, the name i told u what was it | S |
| elliptic | my name?, name of mine you know? | S |
| with context (the name said earlier in the session) | "my name is Ben. whats my name" | S |

## thanks (chat.thanks)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bare | thanks, thank you, thx, ty, tysm, cheers, ta, many thanks | S |
| typos | thnks, thnx, thanx, thanku, tks, tnx, thankz | S |
| intensified | thanks a lot, thank you so much, thanks a ton buddy, thx a lot | S |
| with the reason | thanks for the help, thank you for helping me, thanks for answering | S |
| with a lead interjection | great thanks, awesome thanks, ok thanks, oh nice thanks a lot, cool thank you | S |
| with a compliment tail | thanks you helped, thanks buddy you are great, thanks you rock | S |
| appreciation | much appreciated, i appreciate it, that was helpful, that helped | S |
| bare compliment ("you are great") | | U (not a thanks; the thanks3 family needs "helpful/useful" words or a thanks word) |

## bye (chat.bye)
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bare | bye, goodbye, see you, see ya, cya, later, farewell, ciao, adios | S |
| abbreviations and typos | gtg, g2g, ttyl, cu, byee, byeee, bai, cyaa | S |
| announcing | gotta go, i have to go, im off, im leaving, time to go, i must go now | S |
| night | good night, nighty night, nite, off to bed | S |
| with a tail | bye for now, bye bye, bye bot, see u later bye, bye have a nice day | S |
| with a lead | ok bye, alright i am leaving, well bye, bot, bye | S |
| two farewell phrases in one message | "Alright, time to go, bye for now." | S (two requests, one per clause, as the dataset targets); without the comma the old canonical target also counts two, which one pattern cannot give: U for the 5 comma-less heldout variants (label artefact) |

## Cross-cutting shapes
| Shape | Status |
| --- | --- |
| very short / elliptic | S (see above) |
| voice fillers and run-ons ("um hey so whats your name pls") | S: two filler slots in the sweep patterns, `ok/okay/please/well/um/so` are dropped by the tokenizer |
| typos / abbreviations u, ur, yr, pls, plz, thx, whats, wat, rn | S |
| pronouns / references | n/a for chat acts; `chat.myname` reads the name stored by an earlier `chat.meet` (S) |
| numbers, units | n/a |
| negation / undo | "do not say hello", "I don't need help" are not chat acts (negative tests) |
| coordination | "hello, what is your name?", "thanks, bye" give one request per clause (S) |
| politeness | please / pls / could you / would you / can u in front of every question (S) |
| questions about the state | what is my name (S) |
| questions about the options ("what can you do") | U here: answered by `ui.help` |

files.coverage.md:
# kids.shapes: request-shape catalogue (R2)

Status: **S** = supported by general patterns, with tests in `tests.sop` (`t.shapes.*`; `s###` come from the rule sweep); **U** = unsupported, with the reason.
Operations: sides and corners of a shape (ask, yes/no, search by count), describe a shape, shape families (is a square a rectangle), the shape of a thing and the things of a shape, the colour of a thing (ask, yes/no, search by colour), colour kinds (primary, secondary), colour mixing (result, recipe), and teaching facts.

Shared shape rules: politeness and lead-ins (`can you tell me`, `can u say`, `would you say`, `do you think`, `is it true`, `pls confirm`, `i dont get`), tails (`pls`, `thanks`, `lol`, `right`, `isnt it`, `true?`), `a/an/the`, number words, spelling variants of shapes (`sqaure`, `tri`, `rect`, `hexagone` ... in `lexicon.sop`), `color/colour`.

## sides and corners
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | how many sides does a hexagon have / has / on a hexagon, how many corners does a square have | S |
| elliptic / noun first | hexagon sides?, hexagon sides how many, triangle corners how many, sides of a hexagon, sides of a hexagon: how many?, count hexagon sides | S |
| fillers inside | um how many sides does like a hexagon have | S |
| imperative / wish | tell me the number of sides of a pentagon, can you say how many sides a hexagon has | S |
| yes/no | does a triangle have 3 sides, a hexagon has 6 sides right, is a hexagon with 6 sides | S |
| search by count | which shape has 4 sides, shapes with 5 corners, three sided shapes, name a shape with 3 sides, a shape with 3 sides is which one, i need the shape that has 3 sides, 3 sides which shape is that, which shapes have no corners | S |
| "which one has 3 sides" | | U: the word "one" is read as the number 1 by the tokenizer |
| teaching | a triangle has 3 sides, remember a hexagon has six sides, hexagon 6 sides | S |

## describe a shape
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| question | what is a triangle, whats a rhombus, what is an oval like | S |
| imperative | tell me about squares, describe a circle, explain the circle shape, teach me about pentagons, give me a pentagon summary, show me circle facts | S |
| elliptic / noun first | pentagon?, pentagon info, pentagon description pls, hexagon what is it, circles what are they like, a hexagon is what exactly | S |
| confused wording | i dont get what a hexagon is whats one | S |
| comparison ("how is a circle different") | | U: no operation compares shapes |

## shape families
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| aux question | is a square a rectangle, are squares rectangles, does a square count as a rectangle | S |
| elliptic / tag | triangle a polygon?, triangle polygon?, a hexagon is a triangle right, hexagons triangles same?, polygon or not a circle | S |
| lead-ins | would you call a circle a polygon, pls tell me is a square a rectangle | S |
| it-forms | a circle, is it a polygon; is it a polygon, a circle | S |
| round | is a circle round, circle round?, does a circle have a round shape, round is a circle | S |
| abbreviations | is a hexagon a tri, tri is square | S |
| descriptive shapes ("a three-sided shape", "a round shape") as subject | | U: the subject slot takes one noun |

## shape of a thing, things of a shape
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shape of a thing | what shape is a ball, what shape does a ball have, whats the shape of a plate, shape of a clock, plate shape? | S |
| things of a shape | what is shaped like a circle, what looks like a circle, name things shaped like a circle, where do we see a triangle, where can i spot a circle | S |
| teaching | a ball is a circle, a ball looks like a circle | S |

## colours of things
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ask the colour | what color is the sky, what colour is grass, colour of a banana, sky color?, banana colour pls, tell me the carrot color, tomatoes are what color, what colour is a ripe tomato, u know what color a banana is | S |
| yes/no | is the sky blue, is grass green, are bananas yellow, sky blue?, can a banana be blue, a leaf could be blue right, is a blue leaf possible, is the sky supposed to be green, do bananas tend to be yellow | S |
| lead-ins and tags | would you say a banana is yellow, is it true a banana is yellow, pls confirm a banana is yellow, a banana is yellow isnt it, is it blue the sky | S |
| search by colour | which things are red, name something yellow, red things, list objects in red | S |
| teaching | a banana is yellow, bananas are yellow, banana color is yellow, remember that grass is green | S |

## colour kinds
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| aux question | is green a primary color, is red primary, is orange a secondary color | S |
| elliptic | secondary orange?, primary black?, secondary: green?, secondary color green right?, green a secondary one? | S |
| alternatives | is green secondary or primary | S (answers for the first kind named) |
| lead-ins | would you call red a primary color, u think red is a primary color, do u think orange is primary | S |
| list the colours of a kind | which colors are primary, what are the secondary colors, name the primary colours, how many primary colors are there | S |
| "primary colors include orange?" | S |
| "primary color: is red one?" | U: "one" is read as the number 1 |

## mixing colours
| Shape | Examples | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| result | what do red and blue make, red and blue make what, red plus blue?, whats blue plus yellow, mix red and yellow, what happens when you mix red and white | S |
| lead-ins with "if" | if u mix red and yellow what color u get, if i mix red and yellow what color do i get, color from mixing red and yellow? | S |
| elliptic | blue yellow mix?, red yellow mix result, what does red yellow mixing give, whats red yellow | S |
| recipe | how do i make green, how to make purple, which colors make orange, which two colors make brown, how can i make brown paint, orange how made?, what mixes into orange, get orange by mixing what, make orange how, recipe for purple, green is made of what | S |
| wish with "it" | i want purple how do i make it, purple how do i make it | S |
| teaching | red and blue make purple, mixing red and blue gives purple, remember red plus blue is purple | S |
| shades beyond the 12 listed colours, three-colour mixes | | U: only the listed colours and pairs exist in the KB |

## Cross-cutting
| Shape | Status |
| --- | --- |
| very short / elliptic | S |
| voice fillers and run-ons (`um`, `like`, `so`, `wait`) | S |
| typos and abbreviations (u, ur, pls, whats, wat, sqaure, tri, rect) | S |
| pronouns and references ("it", "that one") | S only in the "is it ...?" forms that repeat the noun; U for pure pronoun questions (no shape coreference in the rule formalizer) |
| negation | "a banana is not red" is not a fact to teach (negative tests in `datagen.mjs`) |
| coordination | "a banana is yellow and green" S (two facts) |
| questions about the options | answered by `ui.help` |

files.coverage.md:
# kids.shop — request-shape catalogue (rule formalizer)

**S** = supported, with a test (the `doc=` of `t.shop.swNNN` tests names the class); **U** = unsupported, with the reason. Patterns: `patterns.sop`, rule-sweep families `sw.*` last. Item groups: "N items", "a/the item", "item xN", and pairs of them with and/plus/+/also (single or two items) for every question about baskets.

| Operation | Request shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| money | I have N lei, wallet/purse/piggy bank holds N, started with N | older tests | S |
| money | chat forms: "i got 40 lei in my purse", "40 lei is what i have", "me 40 lei", "im carrying 40 lei", "i only have 40 lei now", "fyi i have 40 lei" | | S: "statement: money in the purse" |
| money | mis-spelled number words ("fourty") | | U: `numbers.mjs` (engine) |
| income | I got / found / earned / received N lei; mom gave me N lei; grandma gave me ... today | | S: "statement: receiving money" |
| expense | I spent N lei; "i paid 2 lei for a sweet", "2 lei gone on candy", "i used 2 lei", "spent 2 lei just now", "i gave 2 lei to the shop", "i lost 2 lei buying a sweet", "minus 2 lei, i bought candy" | | S: "statement: spending" |
| price (statement) | a kite costs 4 lei; "kite 4 lei", "kite cost 4 lei fyi", "remember a kite is 4 lei", "kite price 4 lei", "4 lei for a kite", "btw a kite costs 4 lei" | | S: "statement: price of an item" |
| purchase | I buy / bought; "i just bought 3 pencils", "bought 3 pencils", "i purchased 3 pencils today", "i picked up 3 pencils", one or two items | | S: "statement: buying" (a bare "I bought some stickers" belongs to `kids.tasks`: it ticks an item off) |
| price (question) | "how much does a ball cost", "cost of the ball pls", "price of a ball?", "ball price?", "how much r balls", "how much for a ball", "whats a ball cost", "ball how much" | | S: "price of one item ..." |
| total | N items: "whats the total for three pencils", "pencils x3 how much", "if i buy 3 pencils how much do they cost", "how much for all 3 pencils together", "altogether 3 pencils how much", "whole cost of 3 pencils?", "3 pencils altogether cost?", "how much will i pay for 3 pencils" | | S: "total for N items" |
| total | two items: "how much are 4 kites and a puzzle all together", "altogether 4 kites and puzzle price?" | | S: "total for two items" |
| total | "4 kites + puzzle = ?" (the `+` sign is dropped, no money word is left) | | U: needs the operator or a money cue; engine tokenizer |
| balance | "how many lei do I have now", "lei left in my purse?", "what is my money after shopping", "money left for me?", "after the spending, how many lei", "my purse, how much now?", "my money?", "how many lei in my pocket now", "how much money am i left with", "money i have right now?", "lei count now" | | S: "balance: money left" |
| affordability | "can I buy ...", "could i afford", "do i have the money for", "is my money good for", "enough for ... or nah", "is it possible to buy", "is a puzzle and 2 kites ok for my money", "puzzle + 2 kites, can i pay?", "is my money enough for the puzzle", "i have enough for puzzle?", "is 8 lei enough for a puzzle" | | S: "affordability ..." |
| affordability | "with 11 lei can i get a notebook" (states money and asks in one sentence) | | U: two facts in one sentence; the dispatcher splits it |
| change | "what is the change from 20 lei if I buy a kite", "how much back if i give 20 lei for a kite", "how much will i get back from 20 for a kite", "kite change from 20?", "what do i get back after paying 20 lei for the kite", "if i give 20 lei for a kite whats my change", "20 lei and a kite, what change do i get" | | S: "change from a payment" |
| change | two items: "change from thirty lei, puzzle and 2 kites", "puzzle + 2 kites with 30 lei, change pls", "if i pay 30 lei how much change for a puzzle and two kites", "give me the change, 30 lei, puzzle and 2 kites", "after 30 lei for puzzle and 2 kites how much left" | | S: "change: two items" |
| any question | questions about options ("what can I buy?") | | U: no operation; `ui.help` answers |
| any question | undo / negation ("I did not buy it") | | U: the world keeps facts, not retractions |
| any question | quantities with units other than lei (euro, dollars) | | U: one money unit (leu/lei) |

files.coverage.md:
# kids.tasks — request-shape catalogue (rule formalizer)

**S** = supported, with a test (the `doc=` of `t.tasks.swNNN` tests names the class); **U** = unsupported, with the reason. Patterns: `patterns.sop`, rule-sweep families `sw.*` last (each is generated in three list forms: "my shopping list", a named list without the word list, and the default list). List names that may be said without the word "list" are in `lex.kids.tasks.listnames`.
Routing note: when the active tab belongs to another world (the docs editor, for example), that world's own `list`-patterns win over these (tier 3 of the routing policy). Bare statements about items without the word "list" (`pls add milk`, `homework is done`, `remove milk`) are deliberately low priority because other worlds own the same words.

| Operation | Request shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| add | imperative with verbs add/put/write/pop/jot/stick/..., polite and chat forms | "Please write milk on my shopping list", "can u add milk to my shopping list", "pop milk onto my list pls" | S: "add: verbs, politeness, fillers" |
| add | wish / indirect: "i need milk on my list", "we need eggs on the list", "milk needs to go on my list", "milk should be on the list", "i forgot milk on my list" | | S |
| add | noun-first and list-first: "socks for the garden list please", "socks on the garden list", "garden list: socks", "garden list add socks" | | S: "add: noun-first and list-first" |
| add | list without the word list: "add bread to shopping" | | S: "add: list named without the word list" |
| add | bare "add milk" with no list | | U (deliberate): collides with the editor, music and drawing `add` commands; works on the tasks tab |
| add | coordination of several items / lists in one sentence | "add bread to my shopping list and a book to my homework list" | S through clause splitting (older tests); "milk, eggs and bread" is one item list |
| remove | imperative, "get X off", "take X away from", "toss", "drop", "cut"; polite forms | | S: "remove: verbs and word orders" |
| remove | verbless / noun-first: "milk off the shopping list", "shopping list no more milk", "shopping list minus milk" | | S |
| remove | "remove it" / "that one" (a reference to the last item) | | U: needs the last mentioned item (state in the formalizer) |
| done | statements: "i finished homework", "homework is done", "homework finished!", "all done with homework", "yay finished homework", "done with my homework" | | S: "done: statements" |
| done | tick / cross / mark / check off, strike from: "tick milk off the shopping list", "mark milk done on shopping list", "check off milk on the list pls", "strike milk from the shopping list" | | S: "done: tick / cross / mark" |
| done | "my homework's done", "my X finished" without a verb | | U: `media.music` and `ui.avatar` own "my ...'s ..." sentences by priority |
| not done | "i didnt finish my homework", "homework not finished", "homework still not done", "not finished homework", "no homework finished yet", "i havent finished homework yet" | | S: "not done: negative reports" |
| remind | verbs remind/ping/nudge/alert/notify/alarm, polite, time words ignored (later, tomorrow, tonight) | "nudge me about the dishes later", "ping me to feed the cat" | S: "remind: verbs and prepositions" |
| remind | "dont let me forget to ...", "make sure i remember to ...", "later remind me to ...", "feed the cat, remind me" | | S |
| remind | reminder nouns: "set reminder water the plants pls", "reminder: water the plants", "i need a reminder to ...", "water the plants reminder pls" | | S: "remind: reminder nouns" |
| remind | a real timer / a time of day ("remind me at 5") | | U: no timers; the time word is dropped and the reminder is only listed |
| show list | what is on / show / read / tell me / anything on, with the list word, a list name or the default list | | S: "show list", "show default list" |
| show reminders | "what reminders do i have", "tell me my reminders", "any reminders for me?", "reminders please", "do i have any reminders", "what do you remind me of" | | S: "reminders" |
| lists | "lists i got?", "what kinds of lists do i have", "show all my lists", "which lists exist", "name my lists" | | S: "lists" |
| pending | "whats left on my shopping list", "what is still on the shopping list", "remaining items on shopping list?", "what hasnt been bought yet", "whats left to buy", "still to buy?", "what am i still missing from the shopping list" | | S: "pending: what is left" |
| pending | to do: "what do i need to do still", "what's still open for me", "what's still on my to do", "what do i got left todo" | | S: "pending: to do" |
| count | "how many things r on my list", "hw many things on my list", "how long is my list", "count the things on my list", "number of items on my list?" | | S: "count" |
| count pending | "how much do i still have to do", "how many more things do i need to do", "how many things still open", "how many tasks still todo", "how many chores do we still have" | | S: "count pending" |
| clear | "clear / empty / wipe / erase / reset the list", "list empty it", "make the list blank", "remove everything from the list", "delete everything on the list", "get rid of my shopping list" | | S: "clear a list" |
| has | "is there milk on the list", "do we have milk on the list", "milk on my list or not", "check if milk is on my list", "does my list have milk", "milk on my shopping list?" | | S: "has: is X on the list" |
| check | "did i finish homework", "have i done homework", "is my homework done yet", "homework done or not", "was my homework finished", "could you tell me if i finished my homework", "finished my homework?" | | S: "check: did I finish X" |
| any | questions about options ("what can you do with lists?") | | U: `ui.help` |
| any | undo of the last change ("undo that") | | U: no undo operation |
| any | negated commands ("do not add milk") | | U on purpose: not claimed (negative training examples) |

    ask="What is the item?"

@kids.tasks.entry.progress core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Is it todo, done or removed?"
files.lexicon.sop:
@lex.kids.tasks.triggers core.lexicon
    class=trigger
    doc="Words that signal list requests"
    word=add word=remove word=delete word=clear word=empty word=remind word=reminder word=reminders word=list word=lists word=finished
    word=completed word=done word=tick word=cross word=shopping word=todo word=homework word=left

@lex.kids.tasks.things core.lexicon
    class=unit
    doc="What the lists hold (used in counts)"
    word=thing word=item word=task

@lex.kids.tasks.listnames core.lexicon
    class=noun
    doc="Names of lists that may be said without the word list (shopping, homework, garden ...); listName() in ops.mjs normalizes them"
    word=shopping word=shop word=grocery word=groceries word=homework word=chores word=chore word=errands word=wishlist
    word=packing word=garden word=party word=birthday word=gifts word=presents word=toys word=books word=holiday word=trip
    word=camping word=bedtime word=weekend word=cleaning word=cooking word=pets
files.operations.sop:
@op.kids.tasks.add core.operation
    impl=addItems
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.add
    doc="Adds one or more items (split at commas and \"and\") to a list; items already there are reported, not added twice."

@op.kids.tasks.remind core.operation
    impl=remindMe
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.remind
    doc="Adds an item to the reminders list (no real timer)."

@op.kids.tasks.remove core.operation
    impl=removeItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.remove
    doc="Removes items from one list or from whichever list has them; says when an item is not there."

@op.kids.tasks.done core.operation
    impl=finishItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.done
    doc="Marks an item as done; asks which one when several match; says when it is already done."

@op.kids.tasks.notDone core.operation
    impl=notDone
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.notDone
    doc="The user says they did NOT do something (I didn't buy milk): nothing is ticked off, the answer says so and offers to tick it off later."

@op.kids.tasks.check core.operation
    impl=checkItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.check
    doc="Tells whether an item is done (yes) or still to do or unknown (missing)."

@op.kids.tasks.show core.operation
    impl=showList
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.show
    doc="Lists the items still to do on a list and the items that are done."

@op.kids.tasks.pending core.operation
    impl=pendingItems
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.pending
    doc="Lists the items of a list that are not done yet."

@op.kids.tasks.count core.operation
    impl=countItems
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.count
    doc="Counts the items on a list."

@op.kids.tasks.countPending core.operation
    impl=countPending
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.countPending
    doc="Counts the items of a list that are not done yet."

@op.kids.tasks.has core.operation
    impl=hasItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.has
    doc="Tells whether an item is on a list."

@op.kids.tasks.clear core.operation
    impl=clearList
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.clear
    doc="Removes every item of a list."

@op.kids.tasks.lists core.operation
    impl=showLists
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.lists
    doc="Lists the lists that have items, with their sizes."

files.coverage.md:
# kids.time — request-shape catalogue (rule formalizer)

**S** = supported, with a test (the `doc=` of the `t.time.swNNN` tests names the class); **U** = unsupported, with the reason. Patterns: `patterns.sop`, rule-sweep families `sw.*` last. Abbreviations: day names (mon, tue, tues, wed, weds, thu, thur, thurs, fri, sat, satur; `sun` is not a day abbreviation on purpose: it is the drawing word), month names (feb, febr, apr, jun, jul, aug, sep, sept, oct, nov; jan, mar and dec are not abbreviations on purpose: names and words) in `lexicon.sop`; hr/hrs/min/mins/wk/wks/sec/secs/yr/yrs as literal alternatives of the length patterns.

| Operation | Request shape | Example | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| today / this month / clock statement | "Today is Friday", "It is Friday", "We are on Friday" | older tests | S |
| today | chat forms: "its friday today", "today's friday btw", "fyi its friday today", "hey today is friday", "we are on friday today" | | S: "statement: today is a day" |
| this month | "its May now", "we are in March", "this month is May" | | S |
| clock set | "the clock says 3 oclock", "its 3 oclock now", "the time is 3 o clock" | | S: "statement: it is N o'clock" |
| day/month/season shift | N after: "4 days after Sunday", "whats the day 4 days after sunday", "day that is 4 days later than sunday", "sunday 4 days later is what day", "count forward / skip 4 days from sunday", "if its sunday what day in 4 days", "if i go 4 months past march" | | S: "day shift: N days after", "month shift", "season shift: N after" |
| shift | N before / ago: "count back 5 days from wednesday", "wednesday 5 days ago is what day", "day 5 days before weds", "what day was it 5 days before wednesday" | | S: "day shift: N days before" |
| shift | next / previous: "the day after monday", "next day after monday pls", "after monday which day is it", "before friday what day is it", "u know what day is before friday", "what is the month ahead of may" | | S: "next and previous day", "month shift: before / next", "season shift" |
| shift | today-relative: "what day is tomorrow", "friday today so tomorrow is what" | | S: older tests plus the new "today so tomorrow" pattern |
| shift | sign written as a symbol: "sunday + 4", "march + 4 months = ?", "5 o clock - 30 min" | | U: the tokenizer drops `+`/`-` that follow a word, so plus and minus cannot be told apart (engine) |
| shift | "after spring then two more seasons, which" (the "then ... more" run-on) | | U: counting from a clause |
| month length | how many days in X; "june days?", "days in june?", "whats the length of june", "how long is june in days", "is march 31 days" (answers with the length), abbreviations | | S: "month length ..." |
| span length | "how many hrs in a day", "how many mins in an hr", "in one hour how many minutes are there", "2 wks = how many days", "how many days in a fortnight" | | S: "span lengths ..." |
| span length | bare "24 hours?" / "14 days?" | | U: direction (which unit is the whole) is not given |
| day gap | "days between thursday and sunday", "from thursday how many days until sunday", "how long until sunday if its thursday", "how many more days to sunday when its thursday" | | S: "days between two days", "days until, with today stated" |
| hours gap | "time from 3 oclock to 7 oclock in hours", "3 to 7 hours to go?", "countdown in hours from 3 to 7", "hours from now till 7 if its 3 oclock", "from 9 o clock to noon how many hours" (noon = 12) | | S: "hours between o'clock times", "hours until, with the clock stated" |
| clock arithmetic | + hours: "10 + 4 hours is what time", "ten oclock four hours later?", "in 2 hours from 3 oclock it will be what", "at 3 oclock what time is it 2 hours later" | | S: "clock + hours" |
| clock arithmetic | - hours / minutes: "what was the time 2 hours before 5 oclock", "2 hours ago from 5 oclock what time", "half an hour before 5 o clock", "quarter of an hour after" | | S: "clock - hours / minutes", "clock +- half an hour" |
| reading the clock | "what time r we at", "do u know what time it is", "can u tell me the time", "whats the time", "time pls", "what o'clock is it" | | S: "reading the clock" |
| list weekend / school days | "weekend days?", "which days count as weekend", "name the weekend days pls", "which days are school days" | | S: "weekend / weekday / lists" |
| list days / months / seasons | "name all the days of the week", "list the months of the year pls", "the four seasons?" | | S: "list days of the week", "list months / seasons" |
| season of a month / months of a season | older patterns | | S (older tests) |
| questions about options ("what can you tell me about time?") | | | U: no operation; `ui.help` answers |
| undo / negation | "not Friday" | | U: the world keeps facts, not retractions |
| mixed statement + question in one sentence ("friday is today, just so u know") | | | the statement half works as a separate sentence; run-ons are the dispatcher's job |

files.coverage.md:
# media.music: request-shape coverage (R2)

Every shape a user may use for each operation of the music world, with the test that proves it (`tests.sop`, ids `t.media.music.rNNN`). `supported` lines have a test; `unsupported` lines say why. Shape names: imp = imperative, q = question/request form ("can you ..."), wish = "I want ...", ind = indirect or statement-as-command ("it should be", "too slow"), el = very short/elliptic, voice = fillers, run-ons, typos and chat abbreviations (u, pls, thx, whats), order = word-order variants, syn = synonyms, ref = pronouns and references to the last thing, num = quantities, units and number words, neg = negation, undo = going back, state = questions about the state, opts = questions about the options, coord = coordination.

Shared by every pattern: polite and filler prefixes (can u, could you maybe, hey, um, like, i want, i would like to), trailing fillers (pls, plz, thx, thanks, for me, now, asap, would be nice), number words and digits, and the typo tolerance of the formalizer (spec 03 1b). Songs are recognised by title or nickname (`lex.media.music.songtitles`, `songstarts`).

files.coverage.md:
# ui.avatar rule coverage

**S** = supported (pattern `example=`, `tests.sop` test or `datagen.mjs` family), **U** = unsupported (reason). Earlier tolerance work (commit 861565b: colour/should-be/word-order colour phrasings, comparative size forms, become/make-me characters, noun-first parts, lip colour refusal, clause split) is kept; this sweep adds the rows marked **new**.
Noise handled by the new patterns (`gen`-style prefix and suffix): fillers (`pls`, `plz`, `thx`, `lol`, `rn`, `right now thank you`), modal/wish prefixes (`u should`, `can i have`, `would like`, `i wanna see`), chat abbreviations (`u`, `ur`, `r`, `wat`, `whats`).

| Operation | Request shape | Status | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `setPart` (wear an option) | imperative / wish | S | `wear sunglasses`, `give yourself glasses 3` |
| | chat / statements | S (new) | `u should wear sunglasses lol`, `wear sunglasses right now thank you` |
| | very short | S (new) | `sunglasses pls`, `shades on you please`, `put some sunnies on` (synonyms map to `sunglass`) |
| | on a part | S (new) | `can i have a dish on top of u`, `would like a dish on the top`, `a dish on top would be nice`, `i wanna see a dish on top`, `put a dish up top` |
| `setColor` / `setPartColored` | all earlier phrasings | S | see commit 861565b |
| | misspelt colour (`bleu`) | U | a colour word the lexicon does not know; typo correction does not fix 2 edits in 4 letters |
| `askColor` | question | S | `what colour are your eyes` |
| | chat / word order | S (new) | `wat colour r ur eyes`, `which color are your eyes`, `can you say what color your eyes are`, `tell me the color of your eyes please` |
| `askPart` (kind of hair etc.) | question | S | `what kind of hair do you have` |
| | chat / short (new) | S | `what hair u got`, `hair types?`, `hairstyle?`, `whats ur hair like`, `which hairstyle do you have now`, `tell me ur hair style`, `could u tell me what hair u have` (hair, hairstyle, hair style, haircut all give part `hair`) |
| `hasThing` | question | S | `do you have glasses` |
| | chat (new) | S | `r u wearing glasses`, `u got glasses?`, `is there glasses on you`, `you have glasses or not`, `do u have glasses on` |
| | `glasses on you?` | U | indistinguishable from the command `glasses on you` (no punctuation in matching) |
| `checkMood` | question | S | `are you happy` |
| | synonyms (new) | S | `are u smiling?` (smiling, grinning, beaming map to `happy`) |
| `setMood` | imperative | S | `look surprised` |
| | chat (new) | S | `look surprised pls`, `make ur face surprised`, `i want to see you surprised`, `be surprised please`, `can u make a surprised face` |
| | `show surprise`, `surprise face` | S | kept on the earlier part/surprise patterns |
| `resetPart` | imperative | S | `reset your mouth` |
| | to default (new) | S | `mouth back to normal`, `can u reset ur mouth to default`, `mouth to default please`, `go back to the normal mouth`, `i want the default mouth again` |
| | undo of a change (new) | S | `undo the mouth change` |
| `step` next/previous | imperative | S | `next hairstyle`, `previous mouth` |
| | previous (new) | S | `prev mouth`, `back one for the mouth`, `go to the mouth before this one`, `mouth previous one pls`, `can you go back to the last mouth`, `mouth one step back`, `the mouth from before, please` |
| | next (new) | S | `next hair please`, `try the following hair`, `next hair style for me` (hair forms give part `hairstyle`) |
| `resizePart` | comparatives | S | see commit 861565b |
| `explainSwitch` | `why did you change it` | S | the verbs `do`/`did` were removed from this pattern so that `how come you did not get it` reaches the help world |
| characters, seed, name, animate, listOptions, describe, undo | earlier patterns | S | unchanged |
| negation / undo | `do not change the colour`, `undo` | S | unchanged |

Known gaps: the held-out labels of `show surprise`, `surprise face` and similar ask for `setPart value=surprise` while the world test suite and the person character use `setMood`; the rules keep `setMood` (tests `n47`, `u10`).

files.operations.sop:
@op.ui.avatar.setPart core.operation
    impl=setPart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setPart
    doc="Sets a component by name and by synonym (visor eyes, a dish on top, a medical mask). When only another character has it, the avatar becomes that character. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setPartUnknown core.operation
    impl=setPartUnknown
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setPartUnknown
    doc="A component named with words that are not a known variant: says what is possible. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.step core.operation
    impl=step
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.step
    doc="Next, previous or different variant of a component (dir=next|previous|different). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.resizePart core.operation
    impl=resizePart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.resizePart
    doc="Bigger or smaller (dir=bigger|smaller) for a part. Emoji eyes step along the sizes that really differ (small, pupils, big pupils); the robot and the person cannot scale their eyes, so the answer offers the styles that look bigger or smaller. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.nameOf core.operation
    impl=nameOf
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.nameOf
    doc="The bare name of the avatar. kids.common speaks it as the assistant's name (the avatar and the assistant are one character): ctx.request(\"avatar.nameOf\"). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.resetPart core.operation
    impl=resetPart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.resetPart
    doc="Back to the default variant of one component. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.removePart core.operation
    impl=removePart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.removePart
    doc="Takes off a component that can be absent (mask, glasses, antenna) or a hat. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.removeAll core.operation
    impl=removeAll
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.removeAll
    doc="Takes off everything that can be taken off. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setColor core.operation
    impl=setColor
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setColor
    doc="Sets a color part to the nearest entry of the style palette for a named color. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.shiftColor core.operation
    impl=shiftColor
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.shiftColor
    doc="Makes a color part lighter or darker, one palette step. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askColor core.operation
    impl=askColor
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askColor
    doc="Tells the color of a part in words. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.listColors core.operation
    impl=listColors
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.listColors
    doc="Lists the colors a part can have, or the colored parts of the character. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.surprise core.operation
    impl=surprise
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.surprise
    doc="Random look from a new recorded seed (mode=surprise) or everything different (mode=everything). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setSeed core.operation
    impl=setSeed
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setSeed
    doc="Draws the character from a given seed; the same seed always gives the same look. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askSeed core.operation
    impl=askSeed
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askSeed
    doc="Tells the seed. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setCharacter core.operation
    impl=setCharacter
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setCharacter
    doc="Becomes a robot, a person or an emoji. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askCharacter core.operation
    impl=askCharacter
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askCharacter
    doc="Tells which character is shown. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.listCharacters core.operation
    impl=listCharacters
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.listCharacters
    doc="Lists the characters. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setMood core.operation
    impl=setMood
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setMood
    doc="Sets an expression by mood word, mapped per character. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.checkMood core.operation
    impl=checkMood
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.checkMood
    doc="Yes or no: do I look like that? Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askMood core.operation
    impl=askMood
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askMood
    doc="Tells the mood the expression stands for. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setName core.operation
    impl=setName
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setName
    doc="Gives the avatar a name. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askName core.operation
    impl=askName
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askName
    doc="Tells the name. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.reset core.operation
    impl=reset
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.reset
    doc="Back to the default look (scope=all: all characters, and the robot). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.animate core.operation
    impl=animate
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.animate
    doc="Queues the effect avatar.animate (wave, nod, dance, wink ...): a moment, not stored state. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askParts core.operation
    impl=askParts
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askParts
    doc="Tells what can be changed. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.listOptions core.operation
    impl=listOptions
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.listOptions
    doc="Lists the variants of a component in words. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askPart core.operation
    impl=askPart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askPart
    doc="Tells what the avatar has for a component. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.hasThing core.operation
    impl=hasThing
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.hasThing
    doc="Yes or no: does the avatar have or wear something? Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askWearing core.operation
    impl=askWearing
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askWearing
    doc="Tells what the avatar wears. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.describe core.operation
    impl=describe
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.describe
    doc="Describes the whole avatar in words. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.undo core.operation
    impl=undo
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.undo
    doc="Goes back to the look before the last change (also a change of character). Keeps up to 20 steps in the state. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.explainSwitch core.operation
    impl=explainSwitch
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.explainSwitch
    doc="Apologises and explains a change of character, and says how to go back. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setPartColored core.operation
    impl=setPartColored
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setPartColored
    doc="Sets a component and colors it when the character can color it (a red hat). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

files.coverage.md:
# ui.help rule coverage

Status per request shape: **S** = supported (the example is a pattern `example=` entry, a `tests.sop` test or a `datagen.mjs` family and is checked by `npm test` / `test-world` / the export agreement), **U** = unsupported (reason given).
Chat surface noise handled by every pattern: fillers (`please`, `ok`, `um`, `hey`, `so`), modal prefixes (`can/could you`, `can u`, `tell me`, `i want to know`), suffixes (`pls`, `plz`, `thx`, `for me`, `now`), chat abbreviations (`u`, `ur`, `r`, `wat`, `whats`, `hw`), typos of known words (engine typo correction).

| Operation | Request shape | Status | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.capabilities` | imperative | S | `tell me what you can do` |
| | question / modal question | S | `what can u do for me`, `could you tell me what you are able to do` |
| | very short | S | `capabilities?`, `abilities` |
| | abbreviations | S | `what u can do`, `what r ur abilities` |
| | word order | S | `your capabilities`, `what things can you help with` |
| | indirect wish | S | `i want to know what you can do` |
| | negation / undo | U | no meaning for a question |
| `ui.help` (examples for the tab) | imperative | S | `give me some examples`, `list the commands` |
| | question | S | `what can I say here?`, `what could i say, give examples` |
| | wish | S | `i need examples`, `i want to see examples` |
| | very short | S | `examples pls`, `commands pls` |
| | abbreviations | S | `can u give examples`, `gimme some sample commands` |
| | word order | S | `example sentences?`, `examples for me please` |
| | state / option questions | S | `what are the options`, `what should I try` |
| `ui.help count=1` | imperative / wish / short | S | `give me an example`, `example pls`, `just one example`, `can u give me an example` |
| `ui.helpMore` | imperative | S | `show me more things i can say`, `give me more examples` |
| | question | S | `anything else i can say?`, `what else can I do` |
| | very short answer | S | `more`, `more please`, `next examples please` |
| | abbreviations | S | `can u show more`, `more examples pls` |
| | rephrased | S | `more ideas of what to say`, `different ideas` |
| | ambiguity | S (limit) | bare `more` is claimed by a game hint pattern when a game tab is open (tab tier decides) |
| `ui.helpAbout` | question | S | `what does this tab do`, `what is this screen for` |
| | imperative | S | `explain this tab pls`, `tell me about this page` |
| | word order | S | `this tab what does it do` |
| | modal | S | `could you explain what this tab does` |
| | "what can I do on this page/screen" | S | gold maps page/screen to helpAbout, tab to `ui.help` (kept) |
| `ui.helpMe` | very short | S | `help`, `halp`, `sos` |
| | statement as request | S | `im lost`, `i am lost help`, `help i am lost`, `i feel lost here` |
| | wish / question | S | `i need some help`, `can u help me`, `where do i start`, `what now` |
| | chat / feelings | S | `im so lost right now`, `im confused what now`, `i dont know what to do` |
| | on a game tab | U | the tab game's own `hint` pattern wins (`games.chess` `I am lost` = chess hint) |
| `ui.helpGame` | question | S | `how do I play`, `what are the rules`, `how can I win` |
| | named game | S | `how to play chess pls`, `how do i move in chess`, `tic tac toe how do i start` |
| | imperative | S | `explain chess to me`, `tell me the rules of hangman`, `teach me to play` |
| | wish | S | `i want to learn chess how do i start` |
| | word order | S | `chess how to play`, `chess rules pls`, `rules of chess?` |
| | chat | S | `how u play chess`, `what r the rules of chess`, `can u explain chess rules` |
| | twenty questions | S | `how do i play twenty questions` (digit form `20 questions` handled by twin patterns) |
| `ui.helpHow` | question | S | `how do I change the eyes`, `how can i add a table pls` |
| | imperative | S | `tell me how to draw a circle pls`, `explain how to draw a circle` |
| | word order | S | `draw a circle how`, `i want to draw a circle, how` |
| | chat | S | `how u draw circle` |
| | plural / paraphrased `what` | U | the `what` slot keeps the user's words, no lemmatisation (`draw circles`) |
| `ui.helpWhy` | question | S | `why did you not understand that` |
| | chat / contractions | S | `why u no understand`, `why didnt you get that`, `why couldnt you understand that` |
| | statement + why | S | `you did not understand, why` |
| | what-was-wrong | S | `what did i say wrong`, `what was wrong with what i said`, `which part did you not get`, `which words did you not understand` |
| | "how come" | S | `how come you did not get it` (avatar `why did you change it` no longer takes the do/did verbs) |
| | polite | S | `could you tell me why you did not understand that` |

Known limits: held-out records labelled `chess.hint` for `i am lost` (the label was produced with the chess tab claim) cannot be met by a rule world.

files.coverage.md:
# ui.shell rule coverage

**S** = supported (pattern `example=`, `tests.sop` test or `datagen.mjs` family, checked by `npm test` / `test-world`), **U** = unsupported (reason).
Noise handled by the new patterns: fillers, modal and wish prefixes (`can u`, `could you`, `i want to`, `i wanna`, `lets`, `let me`, `we should`), suffixes (`pls`, `plz`, `thx`, `now`, `for me`, `right now thank you`), chat abbreviations (`u`, `pls`, `hw`), number words (`one point five`, `one and a half`, `half`).

| Operation | Request shape | Status | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.openTab` | imperative | S | `open the chess board`, `bring up the map tab` |
| | wish | S | `i want the chess board`, `i want to see the map tab`, `let me see the editor tab` |
| | modal | S | `can u show me the map`, `could you open up the chess board` |
| | very short | S | `map tab pls`, `chess board please`, `editor pls`, `map` |
| | word order | S | `chess board tab pls` |
| | pronoun "back to the editor" | S | `take me back to the editor` |
| | unknown tab name | S | refused politely by the op |
| `ui.playGame` | imperative | S | `play hangman`, `start tic tac toe` |
| | wish / modal | S | `i feel like playing hangman`, `can u play hangman with me`, `wanna play tic tac toe` |
| | very short | S | `hangman pls`, `hangman game please`, `tic tac toe time`, `hangmen game` (plural alias) |
| | `lets do hangman` | U | claimed by the hangman world (`hm.new`), shell stays out |
| `ui.chooseGame` | question | S | `what games can we play`, `which game`, `what games do you have` |
| | imperative | S | `pick a game`, `choose a game for me`, `show me the games`, `list the games` |
| | wish | S | `i want to play something`, `let me choose a game` |
| | very short | S | `games?`, `game time` |
| | `play something` | U | claimed by the music world (`play something`) |
| `ui.back` | imperative | S | `go back`, `go back to the last one`, `back one tab` |
| | very short | S | `back pls`, `previous screen`, `last tab pls` |
| | indirect | S | `return to where i was`, `take me back to where i came from` |
| `ui.whichTab` | question | S | `which tab am I on`, `where am I` |
| `ui.speaker` on/off | imperative / short / modal | S | `turn on the speaker`, `be quiet`, `mute`, `can you speak to me` |
| `ui.listening` on/off | imperative / short / modal | S | `start listening`, `turn off the microphone` |
| `ui.handsFree` on/off | imperative / short | S | `hands-free mode on`, `go hands-free` |
| `ui.rate` slower/faster | imperative | S | `slow it down`, `lower the speed`, `speed it up`, `increase the speed` |
| | statements as commands | S | `too fast, slow it`, `less fast please`, `not so slow`, `too slow` |
| | very short | S | `slower voice`, `faster voice` |
| | on a music tab | U | the music tab's own tempo patterns win (same words, different op) |
| `ui.rate` value | imperative | S | `set the speech rate to 1.5`, `make the speed 1.5` |
| | very short | S | `speech rate 1.5`, `rate 1.5 please`, `voice speed 1.5 pls` |
| | modal / wish | S | `could you set talking speed to 1.5`, `i want speech rate one and a half` |
| | number words | S | `one point five`, `one and a half`, `one and a quarter`, `half`, `three quarters`, `1,5` |
| | `speak at 1.5` | S | yes |
| `ui.language` | imperative | S | `speak english`, `switch to romanian` |
| | wish | S | `i want english`, `i prefer romanian` |
| | return forms | S | `back to english` |
| | modal / duration | S | `could you use english from now on`, `can u speak english now` |
| | very short | S | `english pls`, `in english please` |
| `ui.newGame` | imperative / short | S | existing patterns (`new game`, `play again`, `start over`) |
| `ui.giveUp` | imperative | S | `i give up`, `quit this game please` (priority 8: the tab game's own resign wins) |
| | stop forms | S | `stop game pls`, `can we stop the game`, `i want to stop the game now`, `stop the game for now` |
| | noun first | S | `game stop`, `game over`, `stop it, game over` |
| `ui.hint` | imperative / short | S | existing (`give me a hint`) |
| | `clue` forms | U | cross-world: the open game's own hint pattern owns `clue` in the labelled data |
| `ui.phraseLog` show | imperative | S | `show my phrase log`, `phrase log` |
| `ui.phraseLog` export | imperative / wish | S | `download my phrase log`, `i want a copy of my phrase log`, `export phrase log` |
| | very short / order | S | `phrase log download pls`, `phrase log to file please`, `download the phrases i said` |
| `ui.phraseLog` count | question | S | `how many phrases have i said`, `how many things have i said so far` |
| | abbreviations / order | S | `hw many phrases i said`, `number of phrases i said`, `count my phrases`, `phrase count?` |
| | polite | S | `tell me how many phrases i said` |
| negation / undo | `do not open the editor`, `never go back` | S (not claimed) | negative datagen families |

Known cross-world limits (engine routing, not rules): the same words belong to several worlds (`slow down` music tempo vs speech rate, `quit this game` chess resign vs shell give up, `pick a game`/`take me back` edited by the editor select pattern when its priority is high; the editor select patterns were kept narrow for that reason).

files.legend.sop:
@legend.user.profile core.legend
    namespace=user.profile
    version=0.1.0
    imports=core
    imports=kids.common
    doc="A profile of the user, built in a game-like conversation: the plan (sections and fields with priority, sensitivity and questions) and what is known. The keys of user.profile.person are the profile fields; their ask is the canonical question."

@user.profile.person core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="The user. Each key is a profile field; values are kept in the world state with their provenance (said or guessed)."
    example="I am a nurse."

@user.profile.person.name core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What should I call you?"

@user.profile.person.address core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="How should I address you?"

@user.profile.person.location core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Where are you based?"

    card=one
    ask="What is your current role?"

    card=one
    ask="Which field or industry do you work in?"

@user.profile.person.org core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Which organisation do you work for?"

    value=string
    card=one
    ask="How many years of experience do you have?"

@user.profile.person.previous core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="What did you do before?"

@user.profile.person.education core.key

    card=one

    card=many
    ask="What are your hobbies?"

    ask="Which topics interest you?"

@user.profile.person.media core.key

    card=many

@user.profile.person.sports core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="Which sports do you like?"

@user.profile.person.learning core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="What would you like to learn?"

@user.profile.person.career core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What are your career goals?"

@user.profile.person.year core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is your goal for this year?"

@user.profile.person.length core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Do you prefer short or detailed answers?"

@user.profile.person.tone core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Do you prefer a formal or a casual tone?"

@user.profile.person.language core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Which language do you prefer?"

@user.profile.section core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A section of the profile (the sections of the CV card)."
    example="Professional"

@user.profile.section.label core.key
    value=string
    ask="What is the section called?"

@user.profile.section.order core.key
    value=integer
    ask="Where does the section come in the CV?"

@user.profile.field core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A planned profile field: where it belongs, how important it is, how sensitive, and how to ask for it."
    example="Current role"

@user.profile.field.label core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is the field called?"

@user.profile.field.section core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which section does the field belong to?"

@user.profile.field.prio core.key
    value=integer
    card=one
    ask="How important is it to learn (1 to 10)?"

@user.profile.field.card core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Is there one value (one) or several (many)?"

@user.profile.field.sens core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="How sensitive is it (none, low, medium, high)?"

@user.profile.field.want core.key
    value=string

@user.profile.field.example core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is an example answer?"

@user.profile.field.q core.key
    value=string
    card=many

@user.profile.field.follow core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is the follow-up question?"

@user.profile.field.followKey core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which field does the answer to the follow-up fill (empty: it is kept as a note)?"

@user.profile.field.followMode core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="When is the follow-up asked (always or unclear answers only)?"

@user.profile.field.ack core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="How can the system acknowledge an answer ({v} the value, {V} capitalised, {A} with a or an)?"

@user.profile.field.needs core.key
    value=atom
    card=one

    value=atom
    card=many

    example="A nurse: that takes stamina!"

@user.profile.reaction.kind core.key
    value=atom
    ask="What kind of answer does it react to (role, hobby, field)?"

@user.profile.reaction.word core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which answer (lexicon form) does it react to?"

@user.profile.reaction.text core.key
    value=string

@user.profile.activity.role core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which role does it imply?"

files.world.sop:
@world.user.profile core.world
    namespace=user.profile
    version=0.1.0
    legend=$legend.user.profile
    imports=world.core
    imports=world.kids.common
    formalization=rules
    language=en
    status=fixture
    tab=profile
    tabTitle="Profile"
    tabAlias=profile
    tabAlias=my_profile
    tabAlias=about_me
    tabAlias=cv
    tabAlias=resume
    tabAlias=my_cv
    tabOrder=90
    tabKind=tool
    title="User profile"
    summary="get to know you and keep your profile"
    doc="Gets to know the user through a short, game-like interview (one question at a time, chosen by priority and by what is still unknown, with warm acknowledgements, skip and pause respected and remembered) and shows what it learned as a CV-like card. The plan (sections, fields, priorities, sensitivity, question phrasings) is in kb.sop; answers are read with patterns, lexicons and the rules of understand.mjs; nothing is sent anywhere and the Profile tab keeps the data in this browser only. Sensitive topics are never asked for and kept only when the user says remember. State lives in ctx.state; the tab renders it. Hand-built platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."
